cards.title: Phone watchlist frozen -- reconnect loop left the socket subscribed to NOTHING; fixed, VERIFIED on device 2026-07-27
cards.notes:
2026-07-27. Server exonerated by measurement (988 ticks/60s on the phone's exact list; REST watchlist/market is a 5-min cache by design). Client bugs fixed in mobile (3 files): stale-onclose reconnect loop (detach-before-close + current-socket guards + onopen subscription replay), missing bulk 'quotes' branch (snapshots were discarded), 4Hz latest-wins tick coalescing (was ~132 cache writes/s). Founder directive: any watchlist active on any device must work -- desktop already per-widget; phone now subscribes the SAME ['watchlist'] query the screen renders (was ['watchlists'].active_id, a diverging cache) + 30s refetchInterval. VERIFY: Mac rebuild -> prices move on the phone; then flip to done. Follow-ups parked: phone list picker (device-local selection, not global active); _do_broadcast_quote awaits clients sequentially (head-of-line risk).

[2026-07-27 VERIFIED] Phone streams again after the Mac rebuild. Reality check from the Mac agent: the phone builds from feat/mobile-app, NOT main -- it did not cherry-pick a2d3f29; it re-implemented the decoupling principle in branch terms (device-local useSelectedWatchlist module store; pager subscribes selected.symbols; useWatchlists 30s refetch). a2d3f29's mobile hunks are the MAIN-tree expression and get superseded by the branch's files when feat/mobile-app merges. ⚠️ origin/feat/mobile-app last pushed 07-10 (3 perf commits) -- the picker + today's fix are UNPUSHED on the Mac; main can only pick them up after a push. ⚠️ Unconfirmed whether the branch also carries the reconnect-loop + bulk-quotes-frame fixes or only the decoupling -- a fresh rebuild alone masks the loop until the next network blip.

[2026-07-27 RECORD CORRECTED per Mac agent, merge round] (1) 5dfa41a CONFIRMED carries the reconnect fixes (detach-before-close, guards, onopen replay, bulk quotes frame) — the 'unconfirmed' caveat above is closed. (2) My 'phone follows the global active list, just correctly now' was true of MAIN's code only: on feat/mobile-app (what the phone builds) the screen renders a DEVICE-LOCAL selected list (picker already built) while the pager subscribed active_id — that mismatch was the second, load-bearing half of the frozen prices, and my 'phone polls main while active is ai-power-energy' observation WAS this bug, not a separate follow-up. The 'phone list picker' follow-up above is therefore already built on the branch. (3) feat/mobile-app merged to main with mobile/ resolved branch-side (supersedes a2d3f29's hunks; adds bid/ask + selected-list decoupling); serv dev-tree uncommitted mobile edits discarded as fully incorporated.

cards.title: Account-scoped snapshot reads no longer fall back to another account -- SHIPPED 2026-07-26
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25 by the audit round; verified against live code, not inferred. db/sqlite.py:494 get_latest_snapshot(account_id=X) falls back to _latest_run_id(broker) when that account has no poll run -- so it can return a DIFFERENT account's snapshot on the same broker (we run 4+ Alpaca/Schwab accounts). trading/exit_engine.py:549 ALREADY guards this fail-closed, with a comment spelling out the hazard (it was the D3 bug: comparing the broker-side UUID instead of the internal acct_ id made the engine skip every position). The two paths that gate real orders do NOT have that guard: trading/risk_engine.py:301 (checks only `is None`) and trading/proposal_intake.py:121 (checks `is not None`, then reads snapshot['account']['buying_power'] straight into sizing).

DELIVERABLE: mirror the exit_engine guard into both callers -- if snapshot.get('account_id') != the requested account id, treat as NO snapshot (fail-closed, same as today's None branch). Compare the INTERNAL account id, not snapshot['account']['id'] (that is the broker-side UUID and never equals a ledger acct_ id -- getting this backwards is exactly what broke exit_engine for weeks). Plus a regression test per caller.

SAFETY: touches trading/ -- MANDATORY two parallel Opus reviewers with SPLIT mandates before commit (review-agents-opus). Small diff, high stakes: today a mis-sized order is gated by RiskEngine caps, so the realistic blast radius is a wrong-sized (not unbounded) order plus a wrong buying-power ceiling.

[2026-07-26 SHIPPED] Fixed CENTRALLY in db/sqlite.py rather than by copying the exit_engine guard into each caller -- ~11 non-test call sites pass account_id and most have no business knowing about poll-run keying. get_latest_snapshot(account_id=X) now returns X's run or None, full stop.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, and the investigation is why: the first cut KEPT a fallback to an UNKEYED run (account_id IS NULL) on the theory that it meant 'legacy single-account database'. Both reviewers attacked it and the adversarial one was right -- api/main.py:_poll_broker writes account_id=None whenever a broker has no default trade account, and NO Schwab account has is_default=1, so every Schwab poll would write NULL rows; it probed a paper Alpaca ask resolving to a SCHWAB run, i.e. across the paper/real firewall. What settled it: db/multi_account.py:295 BACKFILLS poll_runs.account_id during migration, so a legacy database is keyed by the migration itself and the unkeyed state cannot persist. The fallback defended a state that does not exist (live: 211,637 rows, 0 NULL). Dropped entirely -- which also mooted the reviewer's 37.6ms query-plan finding and the docstring fix, since the helper is gone.

Also shipped: (a) a defense-in-depth guard IN RiskEngine.validate rejecting a snapshot whose account_id != intent.account_id -- unreachable by construction now, which is exactly why it is TESTED by monkeypatching the data layer to regress; the equivalent exit_engine guard shipped INVERTED once and skipped every position for weeks (D3/#91), so an untested invariant here is not hypothetical. (b) tests/test_exit_engine.py gained a test exercising exit_engine's OWN guard -- the existing one now passes vacuously because the data layer returns None before the guard is reached.

BUG THE FIX EXPOSED (reviewer B, HIGH, user-visible): signals/sector_breakdown.py:_resolve_positions kept a LOCAL copy of the aggregate-scope token list that omitted 'overview' -- the workspace selector's DEFAULT value -- and 'all_paper'. Both were resolved as trade-account ids, so they only ever worked by borrowing a random account's snapshot through the very fallback being removed. Sector Radar would have silently lost its exposure ring in the default scope. Fixed by promoting db/account_scope._AGGREGATE_REAL to a public AGGREGATE_REAL and importing it, so the exposure half and the realized-P&L half (resolve_perf_scope) read one source of truth; added an all_paper branch over get_all_latest_snapshots().

11 test fixtures seeded UNKEYED snapshots and validated keyed intents -- stale helpers, not a real requirement (production pollers always key alpaca runs). Repaired to key snapshots the way the pollers do. Suite 2,754 green, ruff clean.

FOLLOW-UPS the review surfaced, NOT fixed here (recorded so they are not lost): (1) db/sqlite.py _latest_run_id_for_account ignores its broker argument, so a run can come back RELABELED with the wrong broker -- pre-existing, unreachable today because account ids are unique per account. (2) signals/regime_sleeves.py:789 skips an exit with a bare continue and NO log when an account has no snapshot -- fail-safe but silent; wants a logger.warning. (3) trading/proposal_intake.py:409 returns risk_blocked with no notify, so a book whose poll dies goes quiet rather than loud. (4) trading/order_proposal.py:302 mislabels a sell-to-close as short_open when the snapshot is missing -- cannot execute (RiskEngine blocks on the same None) but produces a misleading approval card.

cards.title: Honesty leak -- perception strips the calibration flags off win_prob, and create_rule claims 'Armed' when it isn't
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25. TWO places the app tells the user something it has not earned.

(1) ai/perception/context.py:193 _compact_decision_score forwards win_prob / ev / ci and DROPS sufficient, low_confidence, n_samples, base_rate, brier. It lands at frontend/components/workspace/company-info-sections.tsx:405 as a bare 'Win %' tile with no qualifier. What the live research/artifacts/meta.json actually says about that number: n_samples 447 (below its OWN stated ~1,000 floor), brier 0.2456 vs base-rate brier 0.2486 -- i.e. ESSENTIALLY EDGELESS -- honesty.low_confidence true, trained through 2026-06-04 (five weeks stale). This is the same class as the 2026-07-08 red-team (decision-engine-honesty-redteam): flags stripped at a transport, edgeless win% reaching a surface. signals/push.py:665 does it RIGHT (ships calibration:'unproven' and omits winProb when insufficient) -- copy that contract.

(2) ai/chat/tools.py:1161 create_rule returns 'Armed alert: ...' for a type:'trade' rule, but db/ai_tables.py:1055 force-disables exactly those. The model then tells the user a rule is live when it is not. The force-disable is CORRECT safety (chat must not arm an autonomous order generator) -- the return string is the bug.

DELIVERABLE: carry the honesty fields through _compact_decision_score and gate the UI tile on them (or drop the tile until the artifact is retrained); fix the create_rule return to say the rule was saved DISABLED and why. Tests for both.

FOLLOW-UP (not this card): the decision artifact is stale + edgeless. Retraining or retiring it is a separate question -- see calibration-filter-not-goal.

DONE 2026-07-26. Both fixed; the surface count was THREE, not two.

(1) _compact_decision_score now runs the signals/push.py:665 contract verbatim: insufficient bucket or win_prob None -> ship calibration:'unproven' and OMIT win_prob/ev/ci entirely (absent, not null -- a null key is still something the LLM reasons about). When the bucket IS sufficient the number ships with n_samples + base_rate + brier + low_confidence + ci riding along, inseparably. top_factors survive either way: they are observations, not an accuracy claim. The only consumer of the compacted shape is api/ticker_routes.py -> the 'Our facts' tile, which now reads 'unproven' in dim rather than a bare dash (a dash reads as 'not loaded'; the truth is 'we have no calibrated number for you').

(2) create_rule now returns the real enabled flag and a message that matches it; the tool DESCRIPTION in frontend/lib/chat-tools.ts also claimed 'Creates AND ENABLES ... immediately', so the model was being TOLD the false thing before it ever saw a result -- fixed to name the trade-rule exception. Third surface found while fixing: propose-rule-tool-ui.tsx painted a green 'Armed: <name>' banner from the result alone, so a force-disabled trade rule rendered as armed even with a correct backend. Now keyed to result.enabled.

Corroboration found mid-fix: research/artifacts/README.md ALREADY records this scorer as edgeless ('the generic 22-feature scorer is edgeless (Brier ~= base rate)') and says a strategy proposal should carry its own validated backtest stats instead. And mobile/src/features/approvals/score-meter.tsx was already rendering 'thin data' / 'low confidence' badges off exactly the fields the web path was dropping -- the phone was honest, the desktop was not.

Verified: 2759 passed (pytest exit 0), ruff clean, frontend tsc --noEmit exit 0 (borrowed node_modules -- this worktree has none).

cards.title: Nightly setup scan runs 2-3x per night -- the LLM's own title overwrites the idempotency marker
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25. api/research_jobs.py:183 guards the nightly scan with artifact_exists_by_topic('Setup scan (nightly) -- <date>'), but ai/research/setup_scan.py:1150 saves the artifact as topic=str(report.get('title') or display_topic) -- so the model's own free-text title REPLACES the canonical marker and the guard never matches again. Live proof, all three for ET-day 2026-07-24: artifact 200 'Nightly Setup Scan -- July 24, 2026', 201 'Setup Scan -- Nightly (2026-07-24)', 202 'Setup Scan (Nightly) -- 2026-07-24'. Three backend restarts that evening -> three scans -> DUPLICATE ideas in the calibration ledger (VRT ids 1411 & 1413, KMI 1402 & 1414). History: 7 duplicate runs 07-04, 3 on 07-14, 3 on 07-21, 2 on 07-23. This is the Jul-14 triple-run bug reopened through a different door.

Why it matters beyond noise: duplicates corrupt the idea ledger, and calibration-counts-everything means the ledger IS the measurement instrument. Compounding it, setup_scan registers via the legacy register_ideas(artifact_id, ...) path (setup_scan.py:1169), so dedup_key is NULL on every scan-origin row and the Phase-1 cooldown wall (db/idea_outcomes.py:621) never applies to them.

DELIVERABLE: persist the canonical topic (store the marker separately from the display title, or write the artifact with the canonical topic and keep the model's title as a display field). Add the lane_stats day-counter dedup the options-flow lane already uses so the guard survives a restart. Regression test: two runs in one ET day produce ONE artifact and ONE set of ideas.

DONE 2026-07-26. Root cause confirmed one level deeper than diagnosed: create_research_run() opens the row WITH the canonical topic, then save_research_artifact(artifact_id=...) UPDATEs that same row's topic column to the model's title -- so the marker was correct for the whole duration of the run and evaporated at the instant it completed. That is why the duplicates always followed a restart. FIX (a) api/research_jobs.py: the lane_stats day counter is now the PRIMARY restart-safe marker (day('setup_scan', et_date).ran >= 1), same shape as the options-flow lane in the same file, with the landed-verification; the 'ran' bump moved into _mark_setup_scan_ran so it lands exactly once (it doubles as the silent-lane heartbeat pipeline_audit keys on). The guard no longer depends on anything the artifact writer does. FIX (b) ai/research/setup_scan.py:1150 now saves topic=display_topic, restoring the artifact-topic probe as a genuine second layer; the model's title still rides in report_json and heads the rendered report (ai/perception/resources.py:128 still reads it). Manual scans default to 'Setup scan -- <UTC date>', never the nightly's '(nightly)' marker, so they cannot trip the guard. TESTS: 3 in tests/test_idea_engine_fixes.py 6b-2 -- the load-bearing one reproduces the exact production shape (artifact renamed, in-memory set cleared by a restart) and would have failed before this change. 2762 passed, ruff clean.

FOLLOW-UP (deliberately NOT done here): register_ideas() still writes dedup_key NULL, so the Phase-1 cooldown wall never applies to scan-origin rows. It is not a no-op today -- register_ideas already dedupes against still-OPEN rows on exact (symbol, entry_low, entry_high, stop, origin), which is why the 07-24 duplicates needed slightly different geometry to slip through. Adding dedup_key would start rejecting genuinely-different ideas on the same symbol+direction inside a cooldown bucket, which is a calibration-ledger semantics decision, not an idempotency bug. Wants its own card if we want it.

cards.title: THE unlock -- ~92% of stacks score 'contested', so the REASON lane has had zero candidates for 3 sessions
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25 by the fusion audit; the single highest-leverage incomplete piece in the Decision Engine. reason_runs = 0 rows ALL-TIME. The common assumption is that REASON_EMIT_ENABLED=False is what stops it. That is not the binding constraint -- there are NO CANDIDATES to feed it.

Measured from every score_json in fusion_score_history: archetype scorings 2,592 (07-22) / 3,116 (07-23) / 3,341 (07-24); archetype scorings that are NON-contested: 99 / 0 / 0. Only 617 of 7,790 (7.9%) of ALL 07-24 scorings were non-contested. signals/fusion/investigate.py:533 drops any contested stack, so the shadow gate has admitted nothing since 2026-07-22.

MECHANISM: the contested source is overwhelmingly equity_actor -- ~4,000 dark_pool dots/day arrive two-sided, and conviction = |bull-bear| / (gross + 2.0) (signals/fusion/scorer.py:263,280) stays under CONVICTION_BAR=0.4. Dark pool prints are two-sided BY NATURE; treating that as 'the market disagrees' is a measurement artifact, not a signal.

(!) FLIPPING REASON_EMIT_ENABLED TODAY WOULD LIGHT A LANE WITH AN EMPTY QUEUE. Do this card first.

DELIVERABLE (design round first, then build): either judge `contested` PER-ARCHETYPE-GROUP rather than episode-wide (investigate.py:534 currently rejects on the episode's flag even when the archetype's own groups agree -- 99 archetype-non-contested scorings existed on 07-22 under the same episode-level rule, so the group-level read is not empty), or route dark_pool out of the conviction denominator. Then re-run tools/fusion_rescore_replay.py to re-pick T against a pool that actually has members.

UPSTREAM OF FOUR DEAD SUBSYSTEMS: signals/dossier.py (INERT, idea_dossiers table does not exist live), the REASON lane, idea arming (lifecycle_state NULL on all 1,400 idea_outcomes rows), and attention idea-tiers (flow_hot_lane 110/110 rows are reason='position'; idea promotion can never fire). One fix unblocks all four.

CONTEXT, recorded honestly: the mechanical lane that IS running measures fusion_mech 11 won / 107 lost = 9.3% against a 33.3% breakeven for its frozen 1R:2R template, and llm_conviction 0 won / 8 lost. NOT yet a verdict -- n=118 resolved against 977 still open (540 triggered + 437 pending), and the sample is one rough week for longs, which is exactly the tape that produces '0 of 107 losses ever reached target distance'. Re-read this after a fuller sample before concluding the template has no edge.

[2026-07-26 SHIPPED] Fixed, and the MECHANISM above was WRONG -- recorded so the correction survives. Conviction is NOT the wall: on 07-24, 595 archetype scorings cleared conviction >= 0.4 and 525 cleared the full dual gate (z >= 3.5 AND conviction >= bar). The dual gate is working exactly as the founder calibrated T for -- it admits 2-4 DISTINCT episodes/day (GLD, SPY, TSLA, MU, XLE). Every one was vetoed by the LEGACY check at investigate.py:133, score_dots' binary contested-if-EVER bit: fires when any actor group saw both a bull and a bear dot anywhere in the session, undecayed and magnitude-blind. The Horizon Redesign (07-21 S1) named that the disease and shipped score_decayed to replace it; investigate.py already applied the replacement at line 158 but kept the legacy bit gating AHEAD of it. The two are mutually exclusive by construction -- clearing z >= T needs accumulated mass, and accumulated mass on a liquid name guarantees a contrary print, which trips the bit. Measured over 9,049 archetype scorings on 07-22/23/24: 691 cleared the dual gate, 99 cleared the bit, ZERO cleared both. Hence zero candidates ever.

DELIVERED: deleted the legacy veto (4 lines) -- neither proposed design (per-group contested, or dark_pool out of the denominator) was needed, the correct replacement was already wired. tests/test_fusion_investigate.py: the test that encoded the bug (test_contested_stack_is_not_a_candidate) became test_legacy_contested_bit_does_not_gate (verified RED on the old code) + test_decayed_conviction_is_what_rejects_a_contested_stack. NO founder dial moved: T stays 3.5, CONVICTION_BAR stays 0.4, and tools/fusion_rescore_replay.py was NOT re-run to re-pick T -- the pool is already the size T was picked for.

OFFLINE REPLAY (real evaluate_investigation over stored score_json, in created_at order, budget + opening reserve live): 6 rows across 3 market days -- 07-21 SPY/GLD/TSLA shadow_investigate + MU reserve_deferred, 07-22 XLE, 07-23 TSLA. ~1-3 investigations/session against B=5, zero dropped_budget. Candidates spread across the day (65 of 691 in the 9am hour), so the opening reserve does not strangle it.

PENDING (weekend): live proof needs Monday 07-27 -- fusion_score_history ends Fri 16:04 ET. Check fusion_investigations for new rows + the fusion_would_investigate counter. Follow-up noted, not a card: budget is keyed on the episode's OPENING market_day while the opening-reserve window is checked against the wall clock, so a multi-day episode books spend into an old day's bucket (minor -- spend happens at first decision, and the sticky early-return prevents re-bumps).

STILL GATED: this fills the shadow queue; it does NOT light the four dead subsystems (dossier, arming, attention tiers) -- those key off REASON_EMIT_ENABLED, which stays False and is the founder's flip.

cards.title: Four dot components are registered and enumerated in the scorer -- and no code mints them
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25. earnings_proximity, regime, index_pressure and rvol_ex_prints all exist in fusion_component_groups (live rows confirmed) and in signals/fusion/scorer.py GROUP_COMPONENTS (:22-26) -- and NOTHING writes them. Zero rows each in evidence_dots. The data behind all four is live and fresh: earnings_calendar 4,599 rows (487 future-dated, refreshed daily), regime_macro through 2026-07-23, index_pressure_days through 07-24, and the RVOL scanner runs on a job.

CONSEQUENCE beyond the missing angles: the breadth bonus is capped by len(group_scores) (BREADTH_PER_GROUP=0.5, scorer.py:30), so every episode also UNDER-EARNS breadth. The catalyst and context groups are permanently empty.

DELIVERABLE: one _attach_*() minter per component in signals/fusion/intake.py, following the shape of the working _attach_attention (:391) and _attach_shock (:419). Each is roughly 15-25 lines plus a test. Ship them one at a time, cheapest first.

NEWS IS TRACKED SEPARATELY on card news-catalyst-dots -- it is the largest fully-live orphan (news_items 2,676 rows, sub-minute freshness, a working widget, and ZERO references anywhere in signals/fusion/). Per the academic prior (options-flow-academic-prior: event-adjacent flow is where the signal is), a news dot on an episode is probably the single cheapest real dot-connection available.

This is the connect-the-dots thesis in its most literal form: the angles are collected, they are fresh, and they are not being connected.

cards.title: options_flow_daily frozen since 2026-07-17 -- flow 'unusualness' is judged against a stale denominator
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25. options_flow_daily has 146,795 rows and max(date) = 2026-07-17 -- five sessions stale and widening every day. This table is the UV-2 unusualness DENOMINATOR (db/options_flow.py:389 daily_baselines <- signals/options_flow/scan.py:231), so it degrades a FUSED angle, not an orphaned one: every options_flow dot minted since 07-18 was scored against a baseline that stopped moving.

ROOT CAUSE (verified in code, not guessed): api/research_jobs.py:105 admits _market_session() in ('post','closed','overnight'). The ~00:1x ET run therefore passes the gate, scans an ET day that has not happened yet (live log: 'options_flow EOD: date=2026-07-25 underlyings=40 events=0 daily_rows=0'), and then _mark_options_flow_scanned() consumes the once-per-ET-day dedup (_should_options_flow_scan, :70). The real 16:xx ET post-close run is then skipped as already-ran. The job looks healthy in /health the whole time -- it IS running, it is just running at the wrong hour against an empty day.

DELIVERABLE: drop 'overnight' from the admitted sessions (the intent was clearly post-close), or require events>0 before marking the day scanned. Backfill the missing sessions. Regression test that pins an overnight invocation as a no-op that does NOT consume the day's slot.

(!) A job that runs, logs success, and writes zero rows is the worst failure shape -- /health and the dead-man both read it as alive. Worth asking whether any other lane has the same session-gate + dedup pairing.

[2026-07-26 SHIPPED] Root cause confirmed LIVE, not just in code -- the journal (UTC) shows one run/day at ~04:0x-04:2x UTC = 00:0x-00:2x ET: 'options_flow EOD: date=2026-07-26 underlyings=40 events=0 daily_rows=0'. market_session()'s 'overnight' label spans ET midnight (20:00->04:00), so the 00:1x tick scanned the ET day that had just BEGUN and then burned the dedup slot.

ONSET EXPLAINED (the card did not have this): commit 5c3b623, Sun 2026-07-19, made the flow-EOD dedup restart-safe via the lane_stats ET-day counter. Last good row = Fri 07-17; first missing session = Mon 07-20, the first trading day after. Before it the marker was in-memory only, so any restart between midnight and the close let the real run through and the bug stayed latent. A GOOD fix is what made it permanent.

FIX: the session-name gate is gone. api/research_jobs.py now requires is_trading_day(today_et) AND is_after_close(now_et) -- an ET date is scanned only once ITS OWN session is history (half-day aware via session_close_time; is_after_close alone reads weekends/holidays as after-close, hence the is_trading_day leg). market_session import dropped (orphaned). Second guard: the day's slot is consumed only when daily_rows > 0, so a run that writes nothing retries next tick instead of silently burning the day -- bounded, since the gate now only admits after-close on a real trading day.

TESTS (tests/test_research_jobs.py): overnight tick is a no-op that leaves the slot unspent (RED on the old gate); after-close run scans + marks, which pins that the GATE and not a missing broker is what stops the overnight tick; empty result does not burn the day; Saturday is skipped (also RED on the old gate -- 'closed' admitted weekends too).

BACKFILL DONE: 5 sessions (07-20..07-24) restored via signals/options_flow/backfill.py, 50 symbols, 36,827 rows upserted (ON CONFLICT(occ_symbol,date) DO UPDATE, so re-runnable). max(date) now 2026-07-24, ~7.1k-7.7k rows/day across 41 underlyings.

(!) MEASURED CAVEAT, follow-up not a card: backfilled rows and natively-scanned rows are NOT the same measurement. On the 07-17 vs 07-20 overlap the backfill's summed volume is ~7% of a native day (Alpaca 1Day option bars vs what the live EOD scan records). close_oi IS NULL is the clean discriminator (backfill leaves it NULL by design). This heterogeneity PRE-DATES this round -- only 07-10 and 07-14..07-17 are native, everything older is backfill-scale. Checked before keeping the rows: because daily_baselines takes the 20 most recent dates that EXIST (not calendar sessions), the backfilled days DISPLACE even lower-scale June days, so the baseline mean moves +19% to +36% on the full-window 8-30 bucket (SPY/QQQ/TSLA/NVDA) and n rises where the window was short. Net: keeping them moves the denominator TOWARD native scale. The window self-heals to all-native ~20 sessions after the fix deploys.

(!) NOT DEPLOYED: serv runs /home/mbelli/dev/help_me_trade on main (7e97aa1); this fix is on BeerBelly69/clear-the-board. Monday's 16:xx ET run only happens if the branch is merged + deployed.

cards.title: The copilot is silently web-blind -- SearXNG resolves nothing, and web_search reports success anyway
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-25. curl localhost:8585/search?q=nvda&format=json returns HTTP 200 with results:[] and every engine 'Suspended: HTTP connection error' (bing, brave, duckduckgo, google, startpage, wikidata, wikipedia).

ROOT CAUSE is NAME RESOLUTION, not egress -- measured inside the container: socket.gethostbyname('duckduckgo.com') -> gaierror [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution, while a raw TCP connect to 1.1.1.1:443 SUCCEEDS. Docker's embedded resolver (127.0.0.11) is forwarding to host resolvers captured when the network was created; cf. serv-dns-static-resolv (accept-dns OFF, static resolv.conf).

(!) The container is odysseus-searxng-1 -- it belongs to the ODYSSEUS project's compose, not help_me_trade. Our copilot's only web arm depends on another project's config, which is worth knowing before someone edits it.

DELIVERABLE (two halves, both needed):
(1) INFRA: set dns: on the searxng service in the odysseus compose, or recreate the container so it picks up current host resolvers. Verify with the curl above returning a non-empty results array.
(2) CODE, and this is the durable half: ai/chat/tools.py web_search returns 200 with a capabilities blob and NO error in this state, so the model silently answers without web data -- while ai/chat/agent.py's prompt tells it to use web_search for all news. Make the tool return an explicit error when unresponsive_engines is non-empty or results is empty. searxng-port already records the same lesson from 07-02 and 07-14 (web_search_status only checks the URL is CONFIGURED, not reachable) -- this is the third occurrence of the same silent-starvation shape.

Also note: social sentiment has no perception resource, so web_search is the agent's ONLY social angle. While this is broken it is blind to social entirely.

[2026-07-26 SHIPPED] Both halves done, founder's call: we now run our OWN SearXNG instead of depending on odysseus's container.

INFRA: deploy/searxng/docker-compose.yml + settings.yml (new). Port 8586, NOT 8585 -- odysseus itself waits on that container's healthcheck (depends_on: condition: service_healthy), so stopping it would take down that project; ours coexists and odysseus was left untouched. The fix is an explicit dns: [192.168.8.1, 1.1.1.1] (this box runs a static resolv.conf, tailscale accept-dns off -- see serv-dns-static-resolv). Owning the container does NOT fix this by itself: recreate without pinned DNS and the same failure returns. Image pinned to the same 2026.5.31-7159b8aed tag odysseus verified boots clean (2026.6.2 crashes, upstream #1414); json format enabled (disabled upstream by default, and sources.py calls format=json); bing kept in the general pool as the CAPTCHA fallback -- both adapted from odysseus's config, which hit the same problems on this host.

PROOF, same host + same image + same query, the only difference being pinned DNS: OURS 17 results, only 'brave' unresponsive. ODYSSEUS 0 results, all 7 engines down. In-container gethostbyname('duckduckgo.com') resolves.

CODE (the durable half): _searxng_search now returns (results, health) where health = {reachable, unresponsive_engines} -- it previously DISCARDED the unresponsive_engines array, which is the only thing distinguishing 'every engine is suspended' from 'this query had no matches' on an HTTP 200. web_search classifies the empty case as unreachable / engines_down / no_results, and ai/chat/tools.py returns an explicit error='web_search_unavailable' when the search could not actually RUN -- previously it returned the capabilities blob with results:[] and no error, so the model answered from memory believing it had searched. A genuine zero-match query is still NOT an error. 6 tests across test_research_sources.py + test_chat_brain.py, incl. the live payload shape (200 + results:[] + all engines suspended).

SCOPED OUT deliberately: partial degradation (engines down but results returned, exactly today's 'brave' case) is NOT surfaced -- threading health through the success path changes web_search's return type for 3 other callers, and total blindness was the harmful shape. Worth doing if a second engine starts flaking.

(!) OPEN: .env on serv now points at http://127.0.0.1:8586 (backup: session scratchpad env.bak) but hmt-backend has NOT been restarted -- systemctl needs an interactive sudo. get_searxng_url() reads os.environ first, so the live copilot keeps using the dead 8585 until `sudo systemctl restart hmt-backend`. Also NOT deployed: the code half is on BeerBelly69/clear-the-board; serv runs main.

[2026-07-26 follow-on, same thread] Rate-limit resilience. Founder asked whether we could hide that we are a bot. We cannot and should not: SearXNG ALREADY rotates a Firefox UA pool (searx/data/useragents.json) and brave still answers 'Too many request (suspended_time=180)' -- the majors throttle by REQUESTS-PER-IP, so disguise is not the lever and detection evasion was declined. Two legitimate fixes shipped instead:

(1) PACING at the chokepoint. ai/research/sources.py: _pace_outbound_search() enforces SEARXNG_MIN_INTERVAL_S (default 1.5s, env-tunable) inside _searxng_search -- the single point that makes the HTTP call, so every caller is paced without each one remembering to. Root cause was ours: specialists.py:236 _collect_web_for_queries loops queries back-to-back with zero spacing, across specialists AND rounds, which is exactly what flagged this IP on 07-14 (brave throttled, duckduckgo + startpage CAPTCHA). Deliberately serialized -- all callers share one egress IP, so one global gap is the honest model; cost is an interactive chat search can queue behind a research pass. 2 tests (deterministic, fake clock -- no wall-clock sleeps in the suite).

(2) MOJEEK enabled in deploy/searxng/settings.yml (disabled: true upstream). Independent index, not a Bing/Google reseller, does not throttle this host. Resilience via ENGINE DIVERSITY, same reasoning that put bing in the pool on 07-14.

MEASURED: 16 results -> 30 (startpage 10, bing 10, duckduckgo 10, mojeek 10); brave still throttled and now costs us nothing. Container recreated with `docker compose down -v && up -d` because the entrypoint only regenerates /etc/searxng/settings.yml when it is empty or still holds the placeholder -- a plain restart will NOT pick up template edits (the 07-14 lesson). End-to-end verified through the live checkout's own code path: get_searxng_url() -> 8586, web_search returns 4 real hits, no failure sentinel.

ALSO FIXED: data/settings.json still held research.searxng_url = the dead 8585. env wins so it was not biting, but any path resolving without dotenv would have fallen through to the dead instance. Now 8586 (backup in session scratchpad). Edited the raw file, NOT via load_settings/save_settings -- load_settings returns the effective defaults<-env<-file merge, so a round-trip would bake env-derived secrets into settings.json.

NOT DONE, the remaining option: the braveapi engine (built into SearXNG, api_key + inactive: true) is the sanctioned path to brave -- an identified client with a quota beats any disguise. Needs a signup and carries a privacy tradeoff (queries attached to an account), so it is the founder's call. Probably unnecessary now at 30 results without brave.

[2026-07-26 follow-on #2 -- THE READER, and it was the bigger half] Founder asked about crawl4ai. crawl4ai is a READER not a search engine, and the reader was the broken part: fetch_url was a regex tag-stripper, so deep research read nav menus. MEASURED on 7 live finance pages (fetched once, both extractors over identical bytes): tag strip led with boilerplate 7/7 and hit the 4,000-char cap 7/7 -- budget spent before any content. With trafilatura: 1/7 boilerplate-leading, 0/7 empty. NVIDIA press release before/after: nav menu -> 'Record quarterly revenue of $22.1 billion, up 22% from Q3'. (!) favor_precision=True returned EMPTY on 2/7 and an ADVERTISEMENT on 2 more -- worse than the bug; default precision fixed all four. Shipped: _extract_main_content (soft import, latch on IMPORT only) with _strip_tags as the fallback under a 200-char floor. ~37ms/page vs a 15s timeout. trafilatura>=2.0 in requirements.txt + installed on serv. NOT adopted: crawl4ai (headless browser per URL x N sources; fork-storm/RAM history on this box; cheap extractor already recovered 6/7 -- revisit as a measured JS-only tier) and agent search APIs (they replace SearXNG, which is now 30 results for $0 and no key).

cards.title: The spread gate -- is a measured VRP edge reachable once you pay the bid-ask?
cards.notes:
Raised by Study C (IV_HORIZON_BREADTH_PREREG_2026-07-25.md): the wide band (+0.0445) and our own names (-0.0035) sit at nearly identical implied vol (0.554 vs 0.547), so the discriminator is WHICH NAMES, not what IV. Hypothesis was competition -- premium survives where few people sell it, which is where the bid-ask is widest. Every number in Studies A/B/C is vendor MID-market IV and pays no spread at all; a seller sells at the bid.

Pre-registered + committed BEFORE the probe (OPTION_SPREAD_GATE_PREREG_2026-07-25.md). Metric puts the spread in the SAME unit as the edge: half_spread_vol_pts = 0.5 * (ask - bid) / vega, vega rescaled to per-1.00-of-vol, comparable head-on with +0.0445. Instrument verified first -- vendor vega is per-1% as assumed, median vendor/closed-form 0.995 over 262 contracts (a scale error here moves everything 100x).

2026-07-25 RESULT (79 band names, 53 deep, ATM ~30 DTE, calls+puts): BAND median half-spread 0.0870 vol pts = 195% of the edge, 31.2% of premium. DEEP 0.0292 = 66% of the edge, 9.8% of premium. So the premium-carrying names are ~3.2x more expensive to trade than ours -- the competition hypothesis CONFIRMED IN DIRECTION. Only 17 of 79 band names cost less than the full edge one-way, only 4 of 79 less than half of it (what a round trip needs); the tightest, NOW at 0.0189, still eats 42% of the edge in one crossing.

(!) DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED AS A FINDING. The prereg fixed the asymmetry in advance: the probe ran Saturday on Friday's closing book (verified from quote timestamps 19:59:4x-19:59:59Z = 15:59 ET) and closing spreads are wider than intraday, so CHEAP would have been decisive and PROHIBITIVE is not. What survives the caveat better is the RATIO -- both cohorts measured in the same instant under identical conditions -- though illiquid names may widen more into the close, which would exaggerate it.

OPEN: re-run tools/option_spread_probe.py during a live session (Mon 07-27+). Mitigants to read it fairly: the half-spread is a MARKET-ORDER cost and a patient limit captures some of it (but resting at mid in thin names often does not fill -- the same illiquidity being measured); and this is the ATM contract while a wheel sells OTM puts, whose relative spreads are typically worse, so ATM is the friendly case. Does NOT open options-income-lane either way -- the capped-payoff gate is untouched (C4 band 29.7% negative, p05 -0.3105).

cards.title: Options sampler breadth tier — wide IV-only lane so the cross-section is hundreds of names, not 37
cards.notes: Study B (IV_LEVEL_PREREG_2026-07-25.md) measured the blocker precisely: the IV-level effect is real and robust across 2,112 names (+0.0418 even under a 60% IV ceiling) and ABSENT on our own 37 (-0.0004). Not the phenomenon -- the size of the cross-section. So the sampler gained a two-tier universe. deep = the whole banded board + open interest, for names we might actually trade (unchanged behaviour). wide = an IV reading ONLY: a filtered chain slice (expiry window bracketing 30 DTE + strike band at the same +/-25% moneyness), no per-contract rows, no OI call. Measured: ~0.06s and ONE row per wide symbol vs ~0.3-0.9s and ~1,100 rows deep -- breadth is essentially free, depth is what costs. Verified three ways before registering anything: (1) the wide SLICE reproduces the deep BOARD's 30d constant-maturity IV EXACTLY (0.000% deviation across 12 names) because the strike band already contains every strike the ATM interpolation reaches; (2) our iv30 agrees with the independent DoltHub corpus on the same session within 2.2% median across 15 names -- and note the offset is CONSISTENTLY POSITIVE (~+2% on all 15), a systematic method difference, so the two sources must never be naively pooled in a level study; (3) a full 627-symbol sweep ran in 63s, 566/574 wide rows carrying a usable iv30 (the 8 misses REFUSED rather than fabricated, per the no-extrapolation rule). Append-only safety: wide registration NEVER demotes a deep symbol (breadth must not cost depth on a name we hold), deep registration promotes a wide one, and both are regression-tested. iv_daily gained a tier column because a wide row's volume/OI zeros are PLACEHOLDERS, not measurements -- a reader must check tier before aggregating anything but IV/HV/VRP. Universe resolver (tools/resolve_wide_universe.py) sources the DoltHub corpus symbol list deliberately: those names already carry up to 7 years of history, so a level baseline exists on day one instead of 2027, and a symbol is registered only if Alpaca actually returns contracts (append-only means a delisted ticker admitted here would sit in the sweep forever). ⚠️ Vendor pages the chain ALPHABETICALLY even with range filters -- SPY on one page came back 7/10/11-DTE only and could not bracket 30 DTE; wide fetches allow 5 pages. This is perception infrastructure, not a strategy gate: it serves IV-level as a labeled angle in the fusion layer regardless of whether options-income-lane ever opens.

cards.title: Kronos probe — ANSWERED: no. Both legs failed, package deleted per pre-registration
cards.notes: Kronos (github.com/shiyu-coder/Kronos, AAAI'26, MIT) = pretrained autoregressive model over OHLCV candles; sampling it many times yields a CONDITIONAL distribution of future paths. Read on the paper: headline '93% RankIC' is 0.0254 vs 0.0138 (factor-scale, Chinese A-shares/SSE 15-min); on return forecasting it beats the best baseline by only 17% (0.0622 vs 0.0533); its best task is volatility, where the runner-up is GARCH at 9% MAE. Every use case has a cheap classical baseline right behind it — so the ONLY question worth asking is whether its conditional path shape beats an unconditional vol-matched block bootstrap. Value if it passes: a cold-start prior for P(target before stop) on a NEW idea type, before the ledger has graded anything (calibration-counts-everything gives us win% only after a track record exists). Probe is PRE-REGISTERED in research/kronos_probe/README.md: 10 symbols, 5-min RTH bars, 512-bar context, H=12 bars, symmetric ±1σ barriers, 3-way outcome, 200 paths/arm, multiclass log-loss with a paired block-bootstrap CI over session dates. PASS iff Kronos's log-loss is lower AND the 95% CI excludes 0 — anything else deletes the package. LEAKAGE is the live hazard (12B candles from 45 exchanges; no stated cutoff; paper tests 2024-07..2025-06): primary window is post-cutoff 2025-09..2026-07, and the SAME harness runs a pre-cutoff 2023 window so the gap between them estimates memorization instead of fearing it. ISOLATION: separate .venv-kronos (torch NEVER in requirements.txt), upstream cloned not vendored, probe reads SQLite directly so it imports zero product code; removal is rm -rf of one directory. Calibration found + fixed 3 real issues BEFORE any scoring: upstream predict() averages its samples and collapses the distribution being measured (we call generate() with the context on the BATCH dim instead); top_p=0.9 truncation made paths 0.61x too narrow (now 1.0 → 0.97x); and our own sigma estimate swept in 7 overnight gaps per 512-bar context, inflating it up to 2.46x worst on high-vol days (barriers.intraday_log_returns). Related but distinct: per-symbol-volatility (EWMA estimator for SIZING) — Kronos is not a candidate there unless this probe passes. NOTE 07-24: the probe's vol leg runs at 5-min/1-hour, which does NOT settle the per-symbol-volatility card's DAILY deferral — vol results don't transfer across frequencies (intraday is dominated by the U-shape neither estimator models). The daily bake-off is its own cheap CPU-only module, research/vol_bakeoff.py (no GPU, no Kronos). SECOND LEG added 07-24 (founder catch: the probe as built would spend a full GPU day without answering the vol question): Kronos's implied sigma is a FREE byproduct of the same rollouts, so the run now also scores it against EWMA and GARCH(1,1) on QLIKE — separate pre-registered rule requiring it to beat BOTH (beating only the weaker baseline is a FAIL), reported independently so neither test launders the other's null; a path-FAIL + vol-WIN demotes to a bake-off input on per-symbol-volatility, not a pass. GARCH refit per point, fail-soft, +8 min on a ~23h run. NEXT: run primary + leakage windows, then PASS/FAIL per the two pre-registered rules. NIGHTLY PASS 07-25 (1h bars, next-session horizon; own pre-registration in NIGHTLY_README.md, committed before scoring): BOTH LEGS FAIL. Path test: Kronos log-loss 1.2483 vs bootstrap 1.0922, delta +0.1561 CI [+0.1150,+0.1973] — CI excludes 0 on the WRONG side, i.e. ~14% WORSE than an unconditional bootstrap. It is a SHAPE failure, not a scale artifact: mean P(timeout) 0.6476 vs 0.6480 (actual 0.5137), so the arms agreed on how often barriers get touched and disagreed on when/which way. Vol leg FAIL: QLIKE Kronos -5.914 vs EWMA -6.618 vs GARCH -6.752 — BUT that is a LEVEL error, not an information failure: one global rescale per arm makes Kronos vs EWMA a dead tie (-0.0025, CI [-0.1011,+0.0824]). Cause is partly ours — calibrate.py samples ONE symbol; T=0.7 read 1.00x on AAPL but the universe median is 0.741 (GOOGL 0.921 .. META 0.604), so calibrate across symbols if this harness is reused. Deliberately NOT re-run: recalibrating after seeing a FAIL is the laundering pre-registration exists to prevent. Leakage window NOT run (pre-registered as conditional on a path PASS). Two parameters INVERTED vs the 5-min probe, both measured before scoring: gaps are SIGNAL at this horizon (H=7 crosses exactly one) so sigma/bootstrap/outcome all go gap-inclusive; and T=1.0 samples 1.38x too WIDE here (5-min was 0.61x too narrow) so T=0.7. Cost measured: 1.08 s/eval point on the 4090 (36.7 min for 2,040 points) — a production nightly would be ~4 GPU-minutes, so cost was never the blocker, decision quality was. BONUS independent of Kronos: GARCH beats EWMA at 1h/next-session (ewma-garch +0.1338, CI [+0.0339,+0.2405]) — does NOT settle per-symbol-volatility, which defers on DAILY bars. NEXT: nothing further chartered for Kronos by this work; the 5-min primary/leakage run on serv is the remaining open question. || CLOSED 2026-07-25 — BOTH configurations FAILED BOTH LEGS, package deleted per the README's own removal rule. NIGHTLY (1h/next-session, 4090, branch research/kronos-nightly 31a94c7+c34c346, merged to main): path 1.2483 vs bootstrap 1.0922. PRIMARY (5-min, serv 2060S, PID 4000604, ~25h, 6,270 pts / 209 session dates / 10 names): path log-loss 1.1564 vs bootstrap 0.9374, delta +0.2189 CI [+0.1855,+0.2551] — excludes 0 in the WRONG direction, and worse than both a uniform guess (1.0986) and a base-rate constant (0.9172). Vol QLIKE -9.3729 vs EWMA -9.6338 / GARCH -9.6108, loses to both. MECHANISM (the keeper): Kronos's vol is RIGHT (median sigma 0.00503 vs EWMA 0.00511, ratio 0.976) but its PATH SHAPE is wrong — mean P(no touch) 0.451 vs realized 0.628, i.e. its rollouts TREND where real 5-min tape CHOPS. Invisible in a fan-chart demo. Reconciles with the paper: RankIC 0.025 is cross-sectional ranking, compatible with zero per-name path calibration. RETIRES the nightly bonus claim that GARCH beats EWMA at 1h — re-scored ewma_vs_garch -0.0230 CI [-0.0538,+0.0083] straddles zero, tilts EWMA; garch-loses-to-ewma-daily stands. RANKING deliberately NOT run: free from the saved records and NOT condemned by the path FAIL, but underpowered by construction (10 names -> SE ~0.023 over 209 dates vs a 0.025 effect) on the hardest possible cross-section (SPY/QQQ + megacaps, one market factor), and an IC that small needs breadth + shorting the chokepoint does not have. Question closed, not deferred. Raw records deleted with the package — reopening costs ~25 GPU-hours; full numbers live in the BUILD_LOG 2026-07-25 row.

cards.title: Per-symbol volatility model → regime perception + vol-targeted sizing (v1, EWMA)
cards.notes: GAP found 2026-07-24 (traced from a GARCH question): the app has ZERO per-symbol volatility — regime perception is one market-wide VIX/curve read (signals/regime.py, FRED, rule-based), and there is NO volatility in the sizing math (mechanical sizing = pure notional_pct/notional_usd via signals/strategy_scan.py:99 _resolve_notional; notional→shares = floor(notional/price) at trading/proposal_intake.py:_size_candidate ~:120). RiskEngine only GATES qty, never sizes it. LLM books self-size (research/book_driver.py notional) and are book_uncapped in RiskEngine (:501); interactive chat hands over raw qty. So the two places vol matters most — per-symbol regime + the sizing seam — are both empty. BUILD SPEC (brief tools/composer-bridge/briefs/per-symbol-volatility.md): v1 estimator = EWMA (RiskMetrics λ=0.94), NOT GARCH — deliberate (clustering is the value; zero deps; deterministic; fail-soft; keyless/multi-user). GARCH(1,1) DEFERRAL NOW SETTLED 2026-07-24 — KEEP EWMA. Ran the daily bake-off (research/vol_bakeoff.py, CPU-only, no GPU/Kronos): 85 symbols, 169,185 symbol-days over ~10.5y of Alpaca daily bars, walk-forward one-day-ahead, QLIKE, paired CI resampled over DATES. GARCH beat EWMA by a mean of just 0.0107 QLIKE with 95% CI [-0.0348, +0.0129] — STRADDLES ZERO, so the pre-registered tie rule (EWMA wins ties as the zero-dependency incumbent) keeps EWMA. GARCH does NOT earn the arch dependency for daily sizing; do not re-open without a NEW pre-registered question (e.g. a specific regime slice, pre-registered, not post-hoc). ⚠ the first run returned EWMA QLIKE 4.4e10 — a BUG, not a result: NBIS/Nebius was halted ~2.5y (636 zero returns/2610 bars), decaying EWMA variance to 1e-9 so one symbol swamped 170k points; fixed with a halt guard + sigma floor applied to BOTH arms. Parts: (1) signals/volatility.py — forecast_vol(symbol, bars)→VolForecast{daily_sigma, annualized, regime calm|normal|storm via self-relative 33/80 pctile, as_of}; fail-soft None below MIN_OBS=40; LOOKAHEAD GUARD = completed daily bars only (drop today's partial bar, daily-bar-baseline-trap), reuse the bar-dated-today pattern from risk_engine._rest_quote_price. (2) trading/proposal_intake.py:_size_candidate — mult=clamp(target_annual_vol/forecast.annualized, 0.25, 1.5) applied to config notional BEFORE floor; MECHANICAL ONLY + opt-in per-strategy vol_target flag (default off, strategy-off-by-default); books+chat EXCLUDED (self-size + book_uncapped amplification risk); fail-soft=identity 1.0; Decimal at the seam; clamp is the safety (storm shrinks, calm capped, RiskEngine still gates — never past a cap). (3) config volatility{enabled:false,target_annual_vol:0.20,clamp_lo:0.25,clamp_hi:1.5,ewma_lambda:0.94} + log vol_regime/vol_annualized/size_multiplier on the candidate (calibration-counts-everything; log never fabricate). SAFETY: the _size_candidate edit is trading/ sizing math — MANDATORY review = TWO parallel Opus reviewers with SPLIT mandates before commit (per review-agents-opus; NOT Sonnet — the brief's original Sonnet note was a stale copy of the CLAUDE.md safety line, corrected 07-24). Ships DISABLED + shadow-first. OUT of scope this round: GARCH/arch dep, HAR-RV, Kelly, fusion/UI regime dot, applying to books/chat. Rollout: shadow (log-only) → paper opt-in on ONE strategy → perception dot (own card). Review before commit = TWO split-mandate Opus. || 07-24 PARKED (founder). GARCH SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, not deferred: the founder ran the bake-off and GARCH did NOT beat EWMA on daily bars (CI straddles 0 over 169k symbol-days; memory garch-loses-to-ewma-daily) — so the planned GARCH-validation follow-up card is CLOSED and never opened; v1 EWMA stands as the estimator. Founder now running a Kronos-vs-EWMA vol test; that thread lives on card kronos-path-prior-probe (do NOT open a second Kronos card). This card parks in `next` until that result lands — if Kronos wins it swaps in behind the SAME forecast_vol() signature, zero rewiring of the sizing seam or the toggle surface (the interface was designed for exactly this swap). || ⚠️ NEW BUILD REQUIREMENT surfaced by the GARCH test: HALTED TICKERS (zero-return runs) BLOW UP EWMA VOL METRICS — a halt drives EWMA variance toward 0, so multiplier = target/~0 explodes and the clamp would UPSIZE a halted name to clamp_hi, exactly backwards. REQUIRED guard in signals/volatility.py: detect degenerate/zero-return runs (consecutive identical closes, or sigma below an epsilon) → return None (regime unknown) → multiplier fail-soft 1.0, plus a regression test. This is a safety guard, not a nicety. || DESIGN CONFIRMED by founder 07-24: control surface = per-strategy `vol_target` toggle (the unit is the STRATEGY, not the trade; default off) under the global `volatility.enabled` master switch (shadow-safe), plus ONE GLOBAL preset dial `vol_target_profile: conservative|balanced|aggressive` replacing the raw numbers (conservative 12%/1.25x, balanced 20%/1.5x, aggressive 30%/2.0x; clamp_lo 0.25x on all three — shrinking storms is never the risky side). Books + chat stay EXCLUDED (self-size / raw qty). Per-strategy profiles and a Strategy Lab UI switch are later extensions, NOT v1 (v1 toggle = a field on the strategy record). || 2026-07-25 SHIPPED (v1 EWMA, disabled). Built: signals/volatility.py (forecast_vol/size_multiplier/is_degenerate, zero deps, Decimal at the seam) + 13 tests; config volatility_enabled(false)+vol_target_profile(balanced); strategies.vol_target column (idempotent migration, DEFAULT 0); wiring in signals/strategy_scan.py + 4 gating tests. 2717 suite green, ruff clean. DEVIATION FROM SPEC (deliberate, and it SHRINKS the safety surface): the multiplier lands in signals/strategy_scan.py on the notional BEFORE it reaches trading/, NOT inside trading/proposal_intake.py:_size_candidate as the brief said — the notional→shares floor math in trading/ is untouched, so this round changes NO code under trading/. Consequence for the mandatory review: the TWO split-mandate Opus reviewers are owed BEFORE ARMING, not before commit — the path is double-gated off (global volatility_enabled false AND per-strategy vol_target 0; resizing needs BOTH), so it cannot alter an order until the founder flips two switches. Halt guard shipped as specified: degenerate/zero-return runs and sub-1bp sigma return None → multiplier fail-soft 1.0, never the clamp_hi upsize the NBIS bug would have caused (regression test test_halted_symbol_gets_no_forecast_and_normal_size). cards.title: Chart bars: incremental refresh + broadened prewarm + reload-persistent frontend cache
cards.notes: Draft PR (worktree). Root cause of 'watchlist charts still slow on some timeframes' (chart perf audit): the prewarm loop re-walked the ENTIRE `days` range on every TTL expiry, so keeping a series warm cost as much as a cold load - which is why prewarm scope had to stay pinned to the 1Day default only (storm invariant, see chart-bars-prewarm-storms). Fix: _fetch_bars now dispatches incremental-vs-full. A warm series with a fresh full baseline re-fetches only a small trailing window (_BARS_INCREMENTAL_DAYS, 2-90d by timeframe) and merges it over the cached bars - still-forming last bar overwritten, new bars appended; ascending same-provider ISO times so the concat stays sorted+deduped. Full re-baseline forced hourly (_BARS_FULL_REBASELINE) so split adjustments / history revisions propagate. Empty window / provider error / inc>=days -> fall back to a full walk (which owns the resilience + stale-if-error fallbacks). ENABLER for #2 (prewarm more than the default timeframe) without outrunning the TTLs. tests/test_bars_cache.py +3 (merge, hourly rebaseline, empty->full); 8/8 module + 53 adjacent green; ruff clean. Deploy + founder verify pending. || FIX #2 (same PR): prewarm now broadcasts the K most-recently-used distinct specs (_BARS_HOT_SPECS_MAX=2, ~the timeframes you're actively in) across the WHOLE watchlist, not just the 1Day default — so switching symbols/timeframes is served warm. This is the seen-specs x symbols cross-product the 07-22 storm forbade, affordable now ONLY because fix #1 makes each warm refresh cheap. Bounded two ways: K hot specs + a hard _BARS_PREWARM_MAX_ENTRIES=160 cap trimmed from the tail (1Day baseline never sacrificed; hot slots go to most-recently-viewed symbols, never an alphabetical SPY/TSLA clip). Cap trims are logged (no silent caps). tests: replaced the old 'no cross-product' pin with 3 new (broadcast, K-bound, entry-cap+recency+log); 10/10 module + 53 adjacent green, ruff clean. Tunable: K and MAX_ENTRIES. Still open: #3 persist frontend bars-cache across reloads. || FIX #3 (same PR, frontend): the in-memory bars cache (frontend/lib/bars-cache.ts) is now mirrored to sessionStorage — rehydrate on load, flush on tab-hide (pagehide + visibilitychange->hidden) — so a full page reload (F5, restored tab) no longer drops every chart to cold. Transparent to callers: fetchBarsCached still applies the TTL, so a rehydrated-but-expired entry refetches exactly as before; the win is instant paint on a within-TTL reload. sessionStorage (not local) = survives reload/same-tab-nav, clears on tab close; all access best-effort/guarded (private-mode/quota -> cold start). Tricky logic (byte-budget eviction newest-first, corrupt-blob tolerance) factored into pure dependency-free frontend/lib/bars-cache-persist.ts + 5 vitest tests (glob broadened one line). 57/57 vitest + typecheck clean. ALL THREE audit fixes now in this PR; #3 backstop budget 3.5MB. || 07-23 MERGED (PR #102 -> 0756de3) after orchestrator line-by-line review + TWO split-mandate Opus adversarial passes (both approve-with-nits). Review fixes committed on main: (1) MEDIUM futures aggregated-timeframe guard — Schwab builds 1Hour/4Hour/1Week/1Month by in-process aggregation with window-dependent bucket stamps, so incremental merge duplicated (weekly/monthly) or downgraded (hourly) the boundary bucket; futures now force full walks for those timeframes (+1 test, guard is futures-scoped — equities still merge); (2) prewarm cap log now reports 1Day-baseline symbols left cold instead of falsely claiming coverage preserved (200+ name lists WOULD cut baseline); (3) parsePersisted now shape-checks data.bars is an array (stale-schema blob would have crashed every chart at data.bars.map; test fixture itself encoded the invalid shape — fixed + 1 test). Deferred follow-ups (reviewer LOWs): backward clock-step bypasses TTL age checks; dev-HMR listener stacking; double-flush serialize on tab-hide; per-key rebaseline jitter (synchronized hourly cohort); truncated tail guard. Deploy + live verify (bars_prewarm lag_s, WAF quiet) pending gauge window.

cards.title: Options corpus captured: DoltHub 7yr snapshot local + verified; forward arm SHIPPED 07-25 (post-close Alpaca sampler, vol+OI)
cards.notes: Founder found dolthub.com/repositories/post-no-preference/options (07-19); verified live via their SQL API: option_chain (per-contract daily EOD bid/ask/IV/all-5-greeks; NO volume/OI) + volatility_history (per-symbol daily iv/hv current + week/month-ago + 52w high/low w/ dates = pre-computed IV-rank ingredients). Depth 2019-02-09 -> 2026-07-17 (updated through last Friday), 1,532 active symbols, sane spot values (SPY .152 / NVDA .417 / TSLA .485). REVISES the 'no free IV history' claim — options lane can open with 7yr context instead of collecting from zero. Plan: (1) import volatility_history ONLY (~2-3M rows, small) into a local store; defer the huge option_chain table; (2) VALIDATION before trust (vendor-model unknown — scraped EOD): run our own snapshot sampler in parallel, compare overlap window vs self-computed IV, spot-check earnings IV run-ups; divergence bounds how much we trust it; (3) coverage check vs watchlist + held names. Does NOT feed the magnet study (no OI). Licensing: research/founder use fine; multi-user serving = derived-data-only rule. Access: SQL API (rate-limited) or dolt clone. Related: options-income-lane (IV-rank gate), options-strategies-direction memory. 07-19 SCOPE EXPANDED (founder: 'a few GBs is nothing to me - what I want is to update and maintain'): full-corpus local copy approved. Probes: corpus is POINT-IN-TIME (TWTR/SIVB/FRC/ATVI all end exactly at delisting; BBBY coverage attrition ~6mo early - margin note); option_chain is near-the-money SAMPLED (AAPL 186 contracts/day not full board) -> est 250-350M rows / 30-60GB. Plan: (1) volatility_history API backfill RUNNING (tools/dolthub_iv_import.py, 1.87M rows -> data/options_iv_history.db); (2) verify count-match + daily --sync cron; (3) dolt clone for option_chain (API cannot paginate it) + daily dolt pull cron; (4) forward superset = our own Alpaca chain snapshot sampler WITH volume/OI (this corpus has neither - no GEX/dealer positioning from it, liquidity proxy = spread width only). EOD granularity: daily-cadence strategies only, no 0DTE/intraday. 07-19 founder sharpened the dependency logic: dolt pull relies on the repo staying alive -> it only insures the PAST (clone is ours forever), never the future. INVERTED: our own daily post-close Alpaca chain snapshot sampler = the LOAD-BEARING appender, starts with THIS round (not later); dolt pull demoted to opportunistic redundancy + free daily cross-validation while upstream lives. Same doctrine as Schwab: use, never depend. 07-19 Databento lead (founder has acct + credits): OPRA.PILLAR statistics schema = per-contract DAILY OI back to 2013-04-01 (May-2025 coverage extension) - the exact gap neither DoltHub (no OI) nor Alpaca (forward-only) covers; would make the magnet/gamma-wall study backtestable 13yrs. Usage-priced per GB by schema; statistics = cheap tier. NEXT: founder drops DATABENTO_API_KEY into .env -> run free metadata.get_cost for 3 scoped variants (index complex / watchlist universe / full) and quote exact $ before any spend. 07-19 RESOLVED: API backfill throttled at bulk scale -> pivoted to shallow dolt clone (data/dolthub_options, 3.4GB TOTAL incl option_chain 113M rows - far under the 30-60GB est). volatility_history extracted to SQLite fast layer (322MB) in 20s, count-verified 1,870,937 exact + 4 spot-rows byte-identical to the live API. Founder simplification: NO standing DoltHub maintenance arm (shallow clones can't dolt pull anyway - ghost-commit limit); snapshot = frozen past; tools/dolthub_iv_import.py demoted to ONE-SHOT gap bridge at sampler-live; tools/dolthub_iv_extract.py = rebuild-after-reclone. IV model continuity plan: rebuild their era under OUR solver from stored per-contract bid/ask (needs underlying closes + rates + dividends - part of the solver build); their IV = cross-check only. REMAINING OPEN on this card: the Alpaca daily chain snapshot sampler (post-close sweep, vol/OI, own unit). 07-19 Databento PURCHASED (founder: 'try just buying 2025 + the old data'): SPX+SPXW OPRA statistics via batch API (streaming 504'd on the 9.5yr window - batch is the bulk path), chunk A 2013-04->2023-01 $19.18/29.2M rec + chunk B 2025-01->2026-07-18 $111.51/170M rec = $130.68 total. CORRECTION 07-19: founder reports ~$88 credit remained -> REVISED 07-20: balance went ~$43 NEGATIVE (batch submit has no funds pre-check; streaming get_range does - a $0.20 SME pull 402'd on the red account, proving both mechanisms). Likely no card charge - portal shows amount due. Founder OK'd the spend ('All good'). SME options statistics (whale's new CME home, $0.20 quoted) waits on a portal top-up. data/databento/OPRA-20260719-{AJ9Q3FL4CR,TPUHTM5E5V}/ (daily dbn.zst, 1.2GB). 2023-2024 middle (~$112) deliberately deferred = 0DTE bundling tax. Verified: 2026-06-30 decodes, OI stat_type=9, symbols map, sane SPX walls (7000/8000 monthlies 175-225k). Jobs re-downloadable 30d. || CLOSED 07-22 board-hygiene pass: capture deliverable complete (7yr snapshot local + verified); the forward Alpaca sample arm is standing infra, not card work. || 07-25 THE FORWARD ARM SHIPPED — and the 07-22 closure was wrong to call it standing infra: it was the load-bearing half (founder's own 07-19 inversion said so) and nothing built it for 3 days while the corpus staled. tools/options_chain_sampler.py + signals/options_chain_snapshot.py + db/options_chain_history.py, cron 20:50 UTC weekdays, own DB data/options_chain_history.db (forward twin of the frozen options_iv_history.db). Per session: per-contract band (|K/S-1|<=25%, DTE<=400) with quotes/greeks/vendor-IV/volume, plus a per-underlying iv_daily row (30d constant-maturity ATM IV, front ATM IV, EWMA HV from signals/volatility.py, VRP, whole-board volume+OI). Universe is APPEND-ONLY (sampler_universe): once sampled a symbol keeps being sampled, because an IV rank is a percentile against that symbol's own trailing year and a watchlist drop would punch a hole the rank averages over. TWO VENDOR TRAPS measured live and closed: (1) dailyBar is the contract's LAST TRADED session, not the session sampled — SPY carried 10,802 bars but only 5,038 were stamped 07-24, so reading dailyBar.v as session volume invents trades for the other 5,764; volume now counts only on a date match. (2) open interest publishes ONE SESSION IN ARREARS (open_interest_date=07-23 on 07-25), so each run writes OI back onto the row for the session it describes rather than stamping it on today — newest session's OI is legitimately NULL until the next run, never quietly wrong. Also closed: --session in the past is REFUSED (exit 2) unless --allow-backdate, because snapshots are live-only and a backdated run stores today's chain under an old date (observed writing bar_date=07-24 onto 07-23 rows). Refuse-don't-fabricate throughout: ATM IV will not extrapolate past the quoted strikes and the term structure will not extrapolate past the bracketing expiries — NULL instead. Constant-maturity interpolation is linear in TOTAL VARIANCE, not vol (vol-space would bias every IV-rank input; measured 0.327 vs 0.267 on a sloped structure). CROSS-SOURCE VALIDATION vs the independent DoltHub corpus: SPY 0.1566 (ours 07-24) vs 0.1524 (theirs 07-17), AAPL 0.2959 vs 0.3075 — agrees ~3% relative across the gap. HV is deliberately NOT comparable (ours EWMA lambda=.94, theirs simple N-day) — do not report them as matching. Vendor greeks/IV stored as CROSS-CHECK ONLY; raw solver inputs (bid/ask/spot/strike/expiry) stored beside them so the corpus can be re-solved under our own model when the binomial solver lands. Measured cost: full board 66,668 contracts across 10 names in 4.9s; ~25k rows/session at today's 8-symbol universe. Verified live end-to-end 07-25 (OI backfill 7,283 rows), 15 new tests, 2,732 passing. OPEN on this thread: (a) index roots (SPX/SPXW) get no OI — not tradable on Alpaca, so no contracts API; Databento covers them. (b) the 07-17 -> first-live-run gap needs the one-shot dolthub_iv_import.py bridge. (c) IV-rank baseline study on the 1.87M stored rows = the actual gate on options-income-lane. // 07-25 CLOSED (b): bridge ran once and retired -- +7,640 rows for sessions 07-20..07-24, local 1,878,577 = remote EXACT MATCH, and since 07-25/26 are the weekend the corpus now abuts the sampler's first run (Mon 07-27) with ZERO hole. Coverage check at the same time is the finding that outlives the fill: the corpus is a CURATED 2,311-symbol set, not a market -- only 37 of the sampler's 53 names are in it, and the 16 missing are not obscure (QQQ, IWM, GLD, SLV, TLT, ARKK, VIXM + the small caps) even though SPY/DIA/XLF are present. Density rises over time too (~60% of sessions through 2020-22, near-daily from 2025), so trailing-year ranks are honest today for the covered 37 while multi-year percentiles rest on a sampled tail. Those 16 have NO IV-rank baseline until our own sampler banks a year (~2027-07) and must be labelled that way, never ranked against a short window -- scope (c) accordingly.

Does it make sense to just take equity here or involve both equity and leaps or just options… or propose a few options.' Architecture (house style): chain data authors candidate expressions DETERMINISTICALLY — IV rank vs the name's own history, strike/expiry grid, EDGAR event dates, capital required, defined max loss; LLM reasons over + explains each plainly; ledger grades every proposed expression. Dependencies: (1) idea ledger is equity-plan-shaped — premium/option trades need a P&L-based grading basis (grading_basis seam exists: plan|horizon_return -> add an options basis + contract fields); (2) per-name chain/IV sampling — today the sampler is index-only; held + watchlist names need daily IV history for IV-rank to mean anything. Also includes the magnet-composed premium trades (see spx-structural-strikes-study). Design round before any build; possibly the app's most valued capability per founder. 2026-07-19: Schwab /chains STRATEGY mode prices spreads server-side (VERTICAL/STRADDLE/CONDOR/COLLAR + ANALYTICAL theoretical pricing with custom vol/rate) — free candidate-pricing source for this lane, saves reimplementing options math; founder-only (Schwab never a product dependency), gentle cadence (WAF).

cards.title: Options lane — the wheel + covered calls as automated portfolio strats (full ambition, staged by broker tiers + proof)
cards.notes:
Founder 07-19 (correcting the first capture): 'These safety rules are made up. We are going to do everything… just need to make sure it's implemented correctly.' Gates = (1) correct implementation (chokepoint/RiskEngine/paper-first extends to options, never shrinks ambition), (2) broker permission tiers (naked short options blocked at most account levels anyway -> hedged/defined-risk = the practical universe for now), (3) proven before armed (his words: 'we still have to prove this would even work'). FLAGSHIP: the wheel (cash-secured puts -> assignment -> covered calls) as an automated strategy — low broker tier, ships via the strategy framework (disarmed, founder arms, per-strat caps/attribution). Covered calls = natural first increment of the same lane. When-gates mechanical + LLM veto (IV rank vs own history, NO earnings inside expiry via EDGAR, shares/cash coverage, strike vs basis); every idea ledger-graded (premium kept vs upside forgone / assignment outcomes). Agent explains every structure plainly (max profit/loss, assignment, why-now) — the explanation IS the product; founder: with an advisor pointing him right + managing the trade, he'd feel better; possibly the most valued part of the app. ⚠️ Execution chokepoint is EQUITY-ONLY today — options execution = its own increment (RiskEngine assignment/expiry model, Alpaca options PAPER first, dual adversarial review, propose-only, off-by-default). ⚠️ Design round must FORMALLY REVISE the June no-agent-shorts decision record (SHORT_TRADING_FINDINGS.md) — option structures embed short exposure; founder 07-19: not afraid of selling short. Memory: options-strategies-direction.

2026-07-19 IV data-quality gate sharpened (founder q: why a second opinion when we have OPRA?): OPRA carries trades+quotes ONLY — every IV/greek is VENDOR-COMPUTED model output (their inverted price, rates, dividend/American-exercise treatment, snapshot timing). Since the lane's trigger is IV-rank, vendor artifacts = real-money bugs (momentum data-gate class). Primary check = SELF-COMPUTED IV from snapshot bid/ask mids (binomial for American singles) — our model, consistent history; vendor-vs-ours divergence is the alarm. Schwab IV cross-check demoted to optional; Schwab's unique value = strategy-chain spread pricing only.

2026-07-19: IV-rank history may be BACKFILLABLE for free — founder found the DoltHub post-no-preference/options dataset (2019->present daily IV/greeks, 1,532 names, verified live); see dolthub-options-history card for the validate+import round. Forward self-collection still runs (validation pair + OI which the dataset lacks).

2026-07-25 GATE ANSWERED -- NO. The pre-registered IV-rank baseline study ran (References/IV_RANK_BASELINE_PREREG_2026-07-25.md + ADDENDUM_A; BUILD_LOG row). Verdict: this lane does NOT open on a variance-risk-premium premise, and an IV-rank ENTRY GATE is not supported. H1 (premise) failed: mean VRP +0.0205 vol pts, month-block CI [-0.0015, +0.0373]. H2/H3 passed loudly (top-minus-bottom decile +0.0807, Spearman +1.000) and the pre-registered confound test then killed it: sorting by IV LEVEL is equally monotone (+1.000), and in a 5x5 level x rank double sort the rank effect does not survive holding level fixed (pooled within-level +0.0061 CI [-0.0268,+0.0323]; -0.0473 over 7 years) and REVERSES in low-vol names -- inside a quiet name a high IV rank means vol is rising for a reason. Most decision-relevant: on the 37 symbols we would actually trade there is NO VRP (H1 -0.0012), and the control shows the gap vs the corpus is the UNIVERSE (a high-vol curated tail we don't trade), not the horizon. Long-run context: a broad VRP does exist (+0.0306 excluding Feb-Apr 2020) but that one nine-week crash erases ~2 years of it -- precisely the tail a wheel is short. Card stays BACKLOG, now with a measured reason rather than an assumption. If revisited, pre-register the LEVEL axis fresh with the crash tail priced in, not averaged away; do NOT re-open from the headline decile table, which is confounded.

2026-07-25 STUDY B (the LEVEL axis) RAN -- effect is REAL, still not building, and the blocker moved. See References/IV_LEVEL_PREREG_2026-07-25.md. B1 PASS: top IV-level decile VRP +0.0944 CI [+0.0581,+0.1288] over 7 years, +0.1125 excluding Feb-Apr 2020. B2 PASS and it is the exact mirror of what killed rank: level orders VRP inside EVERY rank quintile (pooled +0.0857 CI [+0.0604,+0.1193]). B3 PASS both halves -- BETWEEN/selection +0.0736, WITHIN/timing +0.0858 -- which against rank's failure isolates something sharp: the MAGNITUDE of the deviation from a name's own normal is informative where the ORDINAL rank of it is not (95th percentile can sit 5% or 300% above average; bounded rank stats throw away the part that works). B4 FAIL is why nothing gets built: on our own 37 tradable names top-decile VRP is -0.0004 CI [-0.0269,+0.0253]. Diagnostic: the UNIVERSE binds, not the vol ceiling -- all names under 60% IV still passes (+0.0418 CI [+0.0168,+0.0630], 2,112 symbols), our 37 with no ceiling fails. So premium selling needs materially more BREADTH than the watchlist; the chain sampler's append-only universe is the natural vehicle and costs nothing to widen. B5 FAIL as written but B5 was itself the broken instrument (POST-RUN NOTE on the prereg): dropping the global top 5% of VRP removed 31.6% of the top decile because VRP correlates with the sort axis -- a symmetric 5%/5% trim leaves +0.0586, so outlier-robustness is UNTESTED, not disproven. Pre-registered consequences honored: B4 fail -> record and stop; B5 fail -> gates nothing. Card stays BACKLOG. Successor work, now specific: widen the universe, and model the CAPPED PAYOFF directly (a seller keeps at most the premium while the left tail is uncapped, so mean-VRP overstates capture however it is trimmed).

2026-07-25 STUDY C PRE-REGISTERED + RAN --References/IV_HORIZON_BREADTH_PREREG_2026-07-25.md. Study A's H4 arm (forward RV from OUR bars, 21 sessions, instead of the vendor's 30-session hv_current) ran on 37 symbols -- not a data limit, the code just sourced its symbol list from the sampler universe of the day. Alpaca serves daily bars for any ticker, so the cap was an implementation choice. That leaves the horizon x universe 2x2 with one empty cell: wide+vendor +0.0205, narrow+vendor -0.0105, narrow+own -0.0012, wide+own UNMEASURED. C1 fills it; C2 tests whether the horizon choice is material at all (<= 0.0100 vol pts) on the same (symbol,date) rows; C3/C4 re-run the LEVEL axis and the +0.0418 tradable band at the better horizon; C5 reports the deep tier for the record -- registering ~1,800 corpus names as a WIDE COLLECTION tier widened what we OBSERVE, not what we TRADE, so B4's null on our own names is not superseded. C6 pre-registers the bias this design introduces and it cuts the flattering way: a live bar API cannot serve a delisted ticker, and bankrupt names realize enormous vol (large negative VRP), so their absence biases mean VRP UP -- measured on the vendor panel where both groups exist, flagged above 0.0100. Cannot open the lane either way: the capped-payoff modelling remains the blocker.

2026-07-25 STUDY C RESULTS (1,602,950 obs / 2,200 symbols / 118,608 symbol-months / 2020-01-06 to 2026-06-23; bars for 2,285 of 2,311 corpus symbols). C1 PASS +0.0259 CI [+0.0047,+0.0428] full, +0.0363 [+0.0251,+0.0462] ex-2020 -- but KNIFE-EDGE, not a rescue of H1: Addendum A1's comparable 7-year vendor panel gave +0.0202 CI [-0.0018,+0.0371] (FAIL), and C1's interval is the same WIDTH shifted up ~+0.0057, matching C2's measured horizon effect of +0.0051. A verdict that flips on 0.005 vol pts is not robust; only the ex-2020 arm is non-marginal. C2 PASS gap 0.0051 on 634,118 paired (symbol,date) rows -> horizon immaterial to magnitude, confirming 'universe not horizon' at breadth. C3 PASS Spearman +1.000 monotone across all ten level deciles (-0.0067 at mean IV 0.192 -> +0.0909 at 0.833). C4 PASS +0.0445 CI [+0.0178,+0.0661] on 2,083 symbols under the 60% ceiling vs Study B's +0.0418 -- the tradable-band figure SURVIVES the horizon correction. C5 descriptive and unchanged: our 37 deep-tier names -0.0012 CI [-0.0198,+0.0154], in-band -0.0035. C6 flagged but HOLLOW -- its premise ('a live bar API cannot serve a delisted ticker') is empirically false: BBBY 1,718 bars, WOLF 1,718, FRC 907, SIVB 872, so the blowups are IN the panel; the flag rests on 5 symbols vs 2,200 and those 5 had HIGHER VRP (+0.0583), so the bias runs against the result. ** THE NEW GATE, and it is this round's real output: C4's wide band (+0.0445) and C5's own-names band (-0.0035) sit at nearly identical implied vol -- mean IV 0.554 vs 0.547. Same vol level, opposite sign, so the discriminator is WHICH NAMES, not what IV (intervals overlap slightly -- suggestive, not decisive). Natural hypothesis: competition. Our watchlist is megacap + index ETFs, the most heavily option-sold instruments on earth; the corpus tail is not. If that is the mechanism it is BAD news -- options are rich where few people sell them, which is where the bid-ask is widest, and every number in Studies A/B/C is vendor MID-market IV that ignores the spread entirely. So premium selling now has TWO untested gates: the capped payoff AND the spread in exactly the names that carry the premium. Card stays BACKLOG.

cards.title: SPX structural strikes — gamma-wall/collar overlay + pre-registered magnet study
cards.notes:

Two phases, measurement first: (1) MAGNET STUDY — pre-register metrics (print-lab pattern, prereg = LAW) for pin/magnet behavior: distance-to-top-OI-strike into expiry vs control days, on chain snapshots the index chain sampler already collects daily; (2) CHART STUDY — top-OI strike rails + known-collar annotations + roll-date calendar rendered by our chart engine (top-toolbar control, plain lowercase labels, no pills); overlay states what the study MEASURED, never folklore ('magnet' label only if phase 1 validates). If validated, the tradeable framing is REVERSION (founder 07-19): entry = price EXTENDED away from the validated magnet (displacement band from measured reversion-onset percentile), target = the strike, stop = measured reversion-FAILURE percentile — a fully deterministic plan authored by the study, no LLM levels. Study axes: displacement x time-to-expiry x standing OI, ALWAYS against current OI (roll calendar load-bearing — stale strikes are dead magnets). Magnet BREAK with OI standing = its own trend signal, registered not discarded. Both directions measured; above-magnet (downward-pull) setups surface as perception only — chokepoint stays long-only. Expression = DEFINED-RISK structures only, and only after the options lane exists (see options-income-lane card) — naked short strangles never.
