cards.title: ⚠️ No holiday calendar — a market holiday in the exit window can hold a position THROUGH its print
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-16 while verifying the live deploy. trading/market_hours.py is self-described 'v1 — weekdays only, no holiday calendar' with a `# TODO: Alpaca /v2/clock for holidays` on BOTH is_market_open and is_after_close. And research/strategy_features.py::_trading_days_until is HOLIDAY-NAIVE by its own docstring ('Mon-Fri count... May drift ~1-2 days vs the real calendar'). 
★ WHY THIS IS NOW A FAT TAIL, NOT A ROUNDING ERROR: earnings_drift is LIVE + auto, and its entire safety property is 'exit exactly 1 trading day before the print, never hold through it'. A holiday inside the window makes td OVERCOUNT (it counts the holiday as a trading day) — we think we have 2 days when we have 1. Then ON the holiday, is_market_open() wrongly returns True (it's a weekday), the bmo rule fires at 15:45, and the order QUEUES to the next session's open — **which is the print day**. That is holding through the announcement: the exact event exit_lead_td=1 exists to prevent. 
✅ NOT A RISK THIS SEASON: no US equity market holidays between 2026-07-16 and Labor Day (2026-09-07), so the whole Q2 window is clean. ⚠️ It bites in the Q4-earnings window — MLK Day sits in mid-January. Fix before then; don't let a bad fill discover it. 
FIX: Alpaca /v2/clock (or its calendar endpoint) for the real session calendar, wired into BOTH market_hours and _trading_days_until — they must agree or the two gates disagree about what a trading day is. Cache it; it's static per day.

✅ IN PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (branch fix/market-holiday-calendar): built a pure-Python NYSE calendar (trading/market_calendar.py) rather than wiring Alpaca /v2/clock — keyless/offline (no vendor-account gating, matches the EDGAR ethos) and NO network in the hot scan path where _trading_days_until runs. Algorithmic 10 annual holidays w/ observed shifts + Good Friday (Computus) + an _AD_HOC_CLOSURES set for the un-computable ones (Sandy, Bush, Carter). Verified against known NYSE closures 2010-2026 (18 spot-checks + oracle test). Wired into market_hours.py (all 3 fns) and _trading_days_until. Scope = FULL-day closures only; half-day early-CLOSE times are a documented non-goal (only cost: is_market_open reads True for the 13:00-16:00 tail on ~3 days/yr). LEFT OUT (siblings sharing the naive-weekday bug, lower stakes, follow-ups): brokers/market_clock.py session labels, research/idea_tracker.py idea-expiry. 131 tests green, ruff clean. Pending 1 adversarial review + PR.

⚠️→✅ CI (full suite) caught 1 holiday-anchored test the targeted local run missed: test_exit_evaluators.py::test_earnings_hold_when_far anchored its 'far' earnings on 2026-01-19 = MLK Day, which the calendar now correctly excludes (td 10→9). Moved to a holiday-free Jan span (02→16). Exactly 1 of 2200 tests broke = the calendar change's whole full-suite blast radius. Fixed on branch. | DONE 2026-07-16: #88 merged + deployed; live interpreter verify is_trading_day(2026-01-19 MLK)=False; full-suite CI green (1 test moved off MLK was the calendar's entire blast radius). Half-day early-close hole carded separately (market-hours-half-day-early-close).

cards.title: ⚠️ Half-day early-close defeats the bmo earnings exit — can still hold through a print
cards.notes:
Found in adversarial review of fix/market-holiday-calendar (2026-07-16). The FULL-holiday fat tail is now closed, but a COUSIN survives on early-close half-days (13:00 ET: day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, some July 3s). PRE-EXISTING — the old weekday-only market_hours had the identical hole; the calendar PR neither introduces nor worsens it, it just stops certifying it as safe. 
★ MECHANISM: is_market_open() reads True 9:30-16:00 on a half-day (the calendar counts it a full trading day). The earnings exit's non-amc `lead_td_close` branch (signals/exit_evaluators.py, window hardcoded to 15:45-16:00 ET) only fires when is_market_open AND time>=15:45 — which on a half-day is 2h45m AFTER the 13:00 close. So the bmo exit fires post-close, the day-TIF market order queues to the NEXT session's open = the print day for a bmo reporter. Holding through the announcement, same catastrophic case exit_lead_td=1 exists to prevent. 
✅ RUNWAY: next forward half-days are ~2026-11-27 (Black Friday) and 2026-12-24 (Christmas Eve); July 3 2026 is a FULL holiday this year (Jul 4 = Sat). Fix before the Q4 window. 
FIX (why it's a separate card, not the calendar PR): needs (a) early_close_time(date)->time in trading/market_calendar.py for the ~3 half-days/yr, and (b) the earnings exit window in exit_evaluators.py made SESSION-RELATIVE (fire ~15 min before the ACTUAL close, 12:45 on a half-day) instead of the fixed 15:45. is_market_open should also honor the early close. That's earnings-exit-logic surface, distinct from 'add a holiday calendar'. 
Likelihood is low (needs a held name reporting bmo on the session right after a half-day, at exactly td==1) but it's the same fat-tail class as the parent card — close it before Nov 2026. || DONE 2026-07-22: session_close_time(d) in trading/market_hours.py (13:00 on is_early_close days, else 16:00); is_market_open/is_after_close/last_session_close all per-date close-aware; exit window in exit_evaluators.py now SESSION-RELATIVE (last 15 min before the actual close: 15:45 full day, 12:45 half-day). Tests pin 2026-11-27/12-24 incl. the catastrophic hold-through-print case (half-day 14:00 ET = hold, never a post-close fire). Opus review CONFIRMED + caught C1: market_session() was still 9:30-16:00, which would have stranded equity alerts 13:00-16:00 on half-days once is_market_open flipped — fixed same commit (session_close_time-aware, half-day afternoon = 'post').

cards.title: Notional orders — buy $X worth, let the broker do the fractional shares (chokepoint PR)
cards.notes:
Founder 2026-07-16: 'why not just buy 10000 worth and allow fractional shares'. Correct — Alpaca supports NOTIONAL orders natively (send a dollar amount, broker computes fractional shares; market + TIF=day only, which is exactly our case). It's also what the backtest models: research/portfolio.py sizes per_trade_fraction x equity with NO share granularity at all. 
TODAY: trading/proposal_intake.py:81 does `qty = floor(notional_usd / price)` ourselves; brokers/base.py PlaceOrderRequest has `qty` and no `notional`; the adapter body sends qty only. 
GAIN IS SMALL on deployment — measured at $10k/position over the live sp500: avg **98.8%** deployed, worst 65.0% (NVR $6,498 -> 1 share), 0 names unbuyable => ~+0.24pp CAGR. NOT the reason to do it. 
★ THE REAL REASON — the `qty < 1 -> {'status':'too_small'}` drop (proposal_intake.py:90) is EQUITY-DEPENDENT and biases the recovery. notional_pct=10 means the dollar size SHRINKS with equity: at $100k every S&P name is buyable, but at $60k NVR ($6,498) becomes unbuyable and silently leaves the universe; lower still and AZO/FIX/GWW/SNDK follow. **The strategy's universe quietly narrows exactly when it's performing worst.** Notional removes the failure mode at any account size. 
It also SIMPLIFIES the chokepoint: max_order_value_usd is checked as qty x price today; with notional you compare the dollar figure directly, and the integral-qty guard (risk_engine.py:221) stops mattering. 
⛔ TRAP — do NOT unlock fractional by reusing `intent.rebalance`: that flag ALSO exempts the daily-order + open-order throttles (see the comment on OrderIntent). Marking earnings entries as rebalances would silently disable two risk caps as a side effect. 
SCOPE: OrderIntent -> ExecutionService.submit -> RiskEngine.validate -> brokers/base.PlaceOrderRequest -> alpaca.aplace_order body. That's the sacred path => own PR + TWO adversarial reviewers ([[review-agents-opus]] split mandate). Exits are unaffected (they sell a known qty read from the live position — nothing to size).

✅ IN PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (branch feat/fractional-shares-breadth): shipped as FRACTIONAL-QTY, not native notional orders — a deliberate design pivot. Same outcome (100% deployment, expensive names reachable) with far LESS chokepoint surface: no new PlaceOrderRequest.notional field, no adapter notional branch, and — critically — it REUSES the already-proven fractional-qty path (momentum runs on it, so the submit→fill→managed→attribution pipeline already handles fractional). Because we already fetch a live price in _size_candidate, native notional buys nothing here; and a single source of truth (qty, with notional = qty×price) SIDESTEPS the dual-notional smuggling hole entirely, so the founder-greenlit riskengine-notional-reconciliation card is NOT a blocker (stays valid as independent hardening). 
DESIGN: new OrderIntent.allow_fractional — lifts ONLY the whole-share invariant (risk_engine.py:221), NOT the count throttles (that's the trap the board flagged about reusing intent.rebalance; proven by test_allow_fractional_does_not_exempt_count_throttles). Scoped to percent-of-equity strategies (strategy_scan sets it when notional_pct>0 — today only earnings_drift); static-dollar + phone-proposal + agent-scan paths keep the whole-share floor. 
★ LOAD-BEARING CATCH (found before writing): the EXIT engine floored live_qty (int(math.floor)), so a fractional entry would sell 1 of 1.538 and ORPHAN 0.538 forever (next cycle floors dust→0→qty_below_1→never closes = holds through the print). Fixed: full exits now sell the ENTIRE live qty with allow_fractional; scale-outs + whole-share exits unchanged. 
Files: trading/models.py, order_proposal.py (args→intent plumbing), risk_engine.py (gate), proposal_intake.py (Decimal sizing, 9-dp quantize DOWN, $1 min-notional, fixed int() casts), exit_engine.py (fractional full-exit), signals/strategy_scan.py. 6 new tests + full chokepoint suite green (188 passed), ruff clean. 
RESIDUAL for reviewers: a non-fractionable Alpaca symbol would reject at submit (fail-closed, logged, no position) — near-universal for large caps. Pending TWO adversarial reviewers (chokepoint), then PR.

✅ DUAL ADVERSARIAL REVIEW DONE 2026-07-16 (2 Opus, split mandates). DYNAMIC PROVER: SHIP — 25 attack tests + a 3M-case float round-trip probe + a no-mocks end-to-end dry_run through the real chokepoint; could not break oversell, throttle non-exemption, cap enforcement, or the propose→approve round-trip (all PROVEN-SAFE). STATIC ADVERSARY: SHIP-WITH-FIXES — one real HIGH + both prover NITs, all fixed in-round: (1) HIGH — whole-share AUTO full-exit wired qty "2.0" not "2" (snapshot qty col is REAL → Decimal(str(2.0))=Decimal("2.0")); a decimal-format qty could route a NON-FRACTIONABLE symbol's protective stop-sell through Alpaca's fractional engine → reject → the stop never fills. Fixed: exit qty canonicalized (9-dp quantize on fractional, integer-format Decimal on whole). Hit the common case (all whole-share positions) on the safety-critical sell path — my test missed it because Decimal("10.0")==Decimal("10"). (2) entry sibling — an exact-integer-divide fractional order wired "2.000000000"; now "2". (3) defense-in-depth — the RiskEngine fractional exemption now asserts EQUITY-ONLY (no fractional option contracts; unreachable today but the chokepoint self-defends). +3 regression tests (whole-share exit wires "10"; fractional option rejected; integral fractional wires "2"). 207 chokepoint tests green, ruff clean. PR next. | DONE 2026-07-16: #89 merged + deployed pre-open; proven live at the 09:33 ET scan — 7/7 earnings_drift entries executed as exact-notional fractional qtys (e.g. GEN 374.122109988, PWR 15.641696450), all filled in acct_alpaca_strat1; whole-share wire canonicalization + fractional full-exit shipped in the same round.

cards.title: earnings_drift: does holding ONE EXTRA DAY on AMC reporters pay? (PC experiment briefed)
cards.notes:
2026-07-16. Brief: References/EARNINGS_DRIFT_EXTRA_DAY_EXPERIMENT.md (self-contained, sent to PC). 
QUESTION: exit_lead_td=1 exists ONLY because we couldn't tell BMO from AMC — selling day-of would sometimes land after the print. If a company reports AMC, the print lands hours AFTER that day's close, so we could hold through day D and sell at D's close = ONE EXTRA DAY of drift on a 9-day hold (~+11% more exposure). Never tested. 
★ LIVE FEASIBILITY ALREADY CONFIRMED (this is why it's worth PC time): Finnhub/AV supply the FORWARD session in earnings_calendar.hour — measured live, of 957 future rows **544 (57%) have a known session and 247 (26%) are amc**. And it's AUTHORITATIVE not inferred: companies pre-announce their session weeks ahead ('reporting after market close on July 30'); Finnhub's forward hour IS that schedule. Live design: extra day ONLY where forward hour == amc; fail closed on bmo + the 43% null. No new source, no FMP key, no Yahoo scrape (Yahoo 429s this IP outright — a scraped source that blocks us blocks every future user). 
⚠️ ORCHESTRATOR ERROR WORTH REMEMBERING: I first declared this infeasible because EDGAR can't know the forward session — TRUE but irrelevant; I was checking the wrong source while holding the right one. Worse, I read the 92% EDGAR-vs-Finnhub agreement as 'EDGAR is 92% reliable' when Finnhub was the REFERENCE — all 5 disagreements were EDGAR's filing lag, i.e. **Finnhub was right 5/5**. 
⚠️ THE TRAP for the BACKTEST: it must derive the historical session from EDGAR acceptanceDateTime (Finnhub has no history — rolling 30d window), and that is DIRECTIONALLY BIASED: you cannot file an 8-K before you release, so the stamp is a LOWER BOUND on lateness — ~7% of EDGAR's 'amc' calls (2 of 28) are really BMO filed late. Those get held THROUGH their print in the sim => their extra-day return contains a real earnings gap. CONSERVATIVE direction => the measured value is a FLOOR (live uses Finnhub's clean forward hour). Say it, don't silently correct it. 
DESIGN: (1) add `accepted_at TEXT` to research/earnings.py's schema — store the RAW stamp NOT a derived label (re-derivable under stricter rules without a refetch); reuse signals/earnings_edgar.py::session_hour so live/research can't drift (⚠️ UTC->ET conversion FIRST). (2) arm: exit_idx = jn when amc else jn - exit_lead_td; ⚠️ ONLY when bars[jn]['d'] == next_e exactly (holiday => jn is the day AFTER the report). (3) 4 pre-registered arms incl. **Arm D = extra day on EVERYTHING (deliberately wrong) as the NEGATIVE CONTROL** — if D isn't visibly worse than A, the labelling or exit indexing is broken. (4) THE DIAGNOSTIC: extra-day return close[jn]/close[jn-1]-1 split by label — a true AMC extra day is tight pre-report drift; a false one contains the earnings gap (fat/bimodal). The bmo bucket's same-window return IS a post-report return by construction = a free reference for what a gap day looks like. If amc resembles bmo, the labels are junk. 
Costs unchanged (the arm moves the exit, it does NOT add a trade — do not add a round trip).

✅ RESULT 2026-07-15 (PC, post-main-merge): **THE EXTRA DAY PAYS. SHIP IT.** +0.227%/trade conditional on AMC (block CI [+0.058,+0.402], p=0.005) = a ~25% EV lift on ~half the book; **+0.110%/trade portfolio-wide** ([+0.025,+0.198], p=0.007) ≈ +12% overall. And it's a FLOOR — live uses Finnhub's clean forward hour. Branch: origin/research/decision-engine-data-layer (5719359); runner research/_edgehunt/extra_day_experiment.py. 
★ EQUIVALENCE CHECK PASSED — arm A reproduced the stored validated dataset EXACTLY (n=6,624, mean +0.8900%), so the deltas sit on the real baseline, not a re-derivation. Data: full EDGAR refetch, 53,315 events, 100% stamped; labels 3,235 amc / 3,054 bmo / 335 dmh, zero unknown; the holiday bar-alignment guard bit twice (6,622/6,624). session_hour IMPORTED from PR #86 so backtest and live can't drift. 
★ THE DIAGNOSTIC WORKED — amc extra-day stdev **3.19** (tails -8.65/+9.63) vs the bmo gap-day reference **7.15** (-21.04/+18.19). The amc bucket looks NOTHING like a post-report day => labels clean. And **arm C (contamination-cleaned, 16:00-17:30 filings) matches arm B** (+0.101 vs +0.110) => the ~7% late-filed-BMOs do NOT drive the result. 
★ NEGATIVE CONTROL BEHAVED — arm D (extra day on EVERYTHING) has a HIGHER mean (+1.065; post-blowout names carry positive surprises) but significance DIES (CI spans zero, p=0.25), win rate drops 57.8%->56.3%, variance explodes = a lottery ticket, correctly identified. Confirms the sim genuinely sees announcement risk. 
★★ UNEXPECTED + OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT: **most of the value arrives in the OVERNIGHT GAP into day D** — the day-D-OPEN exit is MORE significant than the close (Δ+0.098 [+0.065,+0.169], p<0.0001 vs p=0.007). ⇒ **the exact intraday exit timing on day D is NOT load-bearing** — we do NOT need market-on-close precision from a loop-driven exit engine. De-risks the implementation. 
⚠️ FOLLOW-UP (does NOT affect this delta — both arms share the same 6,624 setups): the run quantified a long-known gap for the first time — **only 654/909 symbols resolve to a CIK**, so ~28% of the universe (delisted names) has Norgate bars but NO earnings dates => absent from the dataset entirely. **'Survivorship-free' is true of the BARS and NOT of the EARNINGS COVERAGE**; the validated +0.89%/trade is conditioned on 'still listed today'. Direction unknown (acquisitions drift up, bankruptcies down; S&P names are acquired far more often than they fail) and never measured. research/earnings.py:224 has always flagged it ('current EDGAR ticker map — delisted names are expected gaps'; _print_coverage prints 'survivor-gap — do not silently drop in filters'). Fix = predecessor-CIK resolution — the same mechanism as the XOM->CIK 34088 case in [[edgar-free-earnings-source]]. 
⚠️ ALSO: _resolve_cik strips Norgate's delisted suffix (XLNX-202202 -> XLNX) and looks it up in the CURRENT map. Today that fails closed. But if a delisted ticker is ever REUSED by a different company it would silently return the WRONG company's earnings dates — fails OPEN. 
NEXT: implement the live gate — extra day ONLY where the forward hour == 'amc', fail closed on bmo/dmh/null (43% of forward rows have no hour). That's exit_lead_td=0 for amc, 1 otherwise.

✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-16 (PR #86) — the AMC extra-day gate + TWO PRE-EXISTING EXIT BUGS the work exposed. All in signals/exit_evaluators.py — **no chokepoint change**. 
★ MECHANISM (founder's idea, verified): no OPG/TIF field needed. execution_service.py:199 already hardcodes time_in_force='day', and Alpaca's docs say *'Orders not eligible for extended hours submitted after 4:00pm ET will be queued up for release the next trading day'* => submit after the close on jn-1 and the broker fills it at report-day's OPEN. (OPG would have needed a new OrderIntent field AND is REJECTED if submitted 09:28-19:00 ET — the founder's day-order route is simpler and has a wider window.) Everything else was already in place: the exit engine runs inside the 24/7 _poll_loop (api/main.py:529, no market-hours gate); the same loop refreshes the snapshot every 20s so RiskEngine's _SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE=5min gate passes overnight; trading/market_hours.py already exports is_market_open/is_after_close; and exit_engine._exit_in_flight (:109) already blocks a duplicate sell while the order sits queued. 
⚠️ BUG 1 (PRE-EXISTING, FIXED): now_iso() is **UTC**, and today[:10] took the UTC date — which rolls at 20:00 ET. For a Thu print the exit fired **20:01 ET TUESDAY**, queued, and filled at WED's OPEN while the backtest exits at WED's CLOSE. **Live silently forfeited a full session of drift on every trade — live was never the validated strategy.** Fixed: all dates are now the ET calendar date. ⚠️ Subtlety my brief MISSED and the implementer caught: _trading_days_until does its own from_date[:10], so td had to be fed today_key too — fixing only the filter would have left bug 1 alive inside the td computation and looked correct. 
⚠️ BUG 2 (PRE-EXISTING, FIXED): the upcoming filter used strict `>`, so on report day the print date was filtered out => next_e=None => **NO earnings exit at all**, falling through to max_holding_days=15. Fixed to `>=` + an unconditional td==0 `report_day` exit — the backstop never existed before. 
⚠️ A PASSING TEST ENCODED BUG 1: tests/test_exit_engine.py:249 pinned today='2026-06-22T12:00Z' (Mon 08:00 ET, PRE-OPEN) and asserted EXIT. The implementer moved the stamp rather than weaken the rule — a green test asserting buggy behaviour is exactly what pressures the next person into 'fixing' the rule instead. 
RULES (all fail closed — anything not exactly 'amc' takes the non-amc path): td==0 -> EXIT unconditionally (backstop); td==1 + amc -> exit only after the close (queues -> report-day OPEN, capturing the overnight gap = +0.206 of the +0.227); td==1 + bmo/dmh/unknown -> exit only when the market is OPEN and >= 15:45 ET (fills near the close as the backtest models) and **must NOT fire after the close** (a queued day order releases at report-day's open = AFTER a bmo print). 
★ NICE PROPERTY: if the engine misses the AMC after-close window, the report_day backstop fires pre-open on report day and the day-TIF order still fills at that day's OPEN — the same target. The backstop costs AMC nothing; only bmo pays. 
⚠️ OPERATIONAL: the bmo exit window is **15:45-16:00 ET (15 min, ~45 loop passes)**. A deploy/restart straddling it means that name rides to the report_day backstop and eats its print. **Don't deploy in the last 15 minutes of a session.** Widening the window costs ~0.015%/trade (drift ~0.1%/day) if that trade-off is ever wanted. 
VERIFIED: 119 passed exit 0 (exit_evaluators, exit_engine, market_hours_sessions, earnings_calendar, earnings_drift_entry, strategy_scan), ruff clean; both bugs reproduced on the pre-fix code and pinned by regression tests; boundary table proved across a real Tue->Thu week with production-shaped UTC stamps. || CLOSED 07-22 board-hygiene pass: PREMISE KILLED — the bmo/amc hour field is DIRECTIONALLY BIASED (recorded in the EDGAR earnings memory: never use hour to shorten the exit lead). Holding AMC reporters an extra day = trusting that label; experiment dead unless an unbiased hour source appears.

cards.title: earnings_drift: breadth beats concentration (PC-validated) + live enters at the WRONG TIME (47/51 unfaithful)
cards.notes:
2026-07-16. Full brief + results: References/EARNINGS_DRIFT_SIZING_EXPERIMENT.md. 
(1) BREADTH WINS (PC, 6,624 setups): capital-matched 50x5% (35.2% invested) vs live 5x10% (31.3%) -> CAGR 8.35% vs 5.18%, maxDD 17.2% vs 22.7%, Sharpe 0.97 vs 0.54. Concentration is worse in ABSOLUTE terms AND takes only 30% of the signal stream (arrival-order clip). Best Sharpe = 50x3% (0.99, 86% coverage). 3% vs 5% is a risk dial, not a finding. 
(2) RANKING DEAD: blowout_reaction_pct deciles show no gradient (decile 4 ~= decile 9; decile 10 best mean 1.33% but ~1.6sigma w/ fattest variance). Don't build ranking. 
(3) ★ FOUNDER CATCH — LIVE ENTERS AT THE WRONG TIME. Backtest enters at EXACTLY 10 td out (earnings_strategy.py:156, holding always 9d); live fires anywhere in 2..10 (strategy_features.py:340). Harmless in steady state, MASS MIS-ENTRY on cold start — which deploying the EDGAR fix causes. Measured live: of 51 firing, only **4 are at td==10** (CVS/FTNT/IEX/PTC); 47 would enter late, some holding 2d instead of 9d = an unvalidated strategy wearing earnings_drift's badge. FIX: require td_to_next == entry_lead_td. Then today's cohort is 4 (cap never binds), it self-ramps to the validated ~40-50 concurrent, and it fails closed on late-arriving vendor dates. The '51 fires/$510k/needs caps' alarm was a COLD-START ARTIFACT. 
(4) ⚠️ THE PC IS ON STALE RESEARCH CODE — it rediscovered the cost_pct=0.30 double-count that main already fixed (PR #28 research/pipeline-honesty-fixes: CV leakage + next-open fills + embargo + cost single-sourcing). Breadth ranking survives (identical drag across arms) but the other 3 fixes change CONCLUSIONS. git pull on the PC + re-run before trusting anything further. 
BLOCKERS that are NOT real: max_daily_orders=20 is an arbitrary default (global, off-by-one); fractional shares already work (risk_engine.py:221 gates on intent.rebalance, set only by momentum) — and the gate's own comment ('would leave ~24% in cash and drop every name above the per-name budget') is VERBATIM the breadth case. BRK.B/BF.B rejected by _SYMBOL_RE=^[A-Z]+$. 
STILL OPEN: per-strategy P&L for entry_mode='auto' (never journals -> stats_by_strategy n=0 forever) = the prerequisite for measuring this live. See [[per-strategy-attribution]].

✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-16 (PR #86): (a) ENTRY TIMING FIXED — is_earnings_drift_entry now `td_to_next == entry_lead_td` (was the 2..10 band). Proven: td=10 fires (9d hold, matching the backtest), td=2/4/9 no longer do. Safe — the predicate is called ONLY by strategy_kinds.py:77 (live); the backtest uses its own _symbol_setups. (b) PERCENT SIZING — nullable strategies.notional_pct; notional = pct/100 x snapshot portfolio_value, else notional_usd unchanged. FAIL-CLOSED: pct set + no usable equity => SKIP, never fall back to the static dollar amount (sizing a real order off absent equity = the wrong-sized-order failure). Validated 0<pct<=100; wired through routes + Settings UI. Proven against the live snapshot: 3% -> $3,000.09 on $100,002.84 equity; no-snapshot -> None. 102 passed exit 0, ruff clean, frontend typecheck clean. 
⚠️ TWO BRIEF CORRECTIONS the implementer caught (both real): (1) resolving notional after the snapshot at :372 put it AFTER the broker bar fetch, so zero-notional strategies started spending a fetch — moved the SNAPSHOT up to :361 instead (it's a pure local DB read), preserving the early-out. (2) ★ momentum.py:279, regime_sleeves.py:522/978 and session_node_strategy.py:525 read notional_usd DIRECTLY and never reach _resolve_notional — so a percent set on those 4 would have stored a rule that never applied while orders kept going out at the old dollar size. That is exactly the [[alert-style-dead-column]] pathology. Gated instead: server rejects notional_pct for those ids, UI hides the control (mirrors the existing _PROPOSE_ONLY_IDS pattern). Wiring percent into the regime sleeves is a SEPARATE call. 
FOUNDER 2026-07-16: turning the other strategies OFF and running earnings_drift alone in strat1 — which also resolves the account-wide _open_exposure cap contention. Opening a second Alpaca login for 3 more paper accounts (Alpaca caps at 3/login). 
TO ARM the validated breadth config: notional_pct=3, max_concurrent_positions=50, max_deployed_usd=100000 (= equity; mirrors the sim's max_gross_exposure=1.0 — anything higher is leverage the backtest never modelled). NOTE the sim compounds (3% of CURRENT equity); our notional_pct now does too, so this is faithful. 
STILL NEEDED before breadth actually works: fractional shares (trading/risk_engine.py:221 gates on intent.rebalance — SEPARATE safety PR, needs 2 adversarial reviewers) or $3k can't buy NVR/BKNG and ~24% strands in cash; and max_daily_orders=20 (arbitrary, global, off-by-one).

⚠️ CORRECTED NUMBERS 2026-07-16 (supersede the table above): the first PC run double-counted costs. At the true 20bps RT, matched exposure: **breadth 50x5% = CAGR 13.2%, maxDD 13.7%, Sharpe 1.47** vs concentrated 5x10% = 9.3% / 19.8% / 0.92. Both conclusions hold, STRONGER. ★ The double-count was an accidental COST-STRESS TEST at ~2.5x the real assumption and the edge SURVIVED it (8.35% / Sharpe 0.97) — breadth beats concentration at BOTH cost levels, which satisfies the validation gate's sensitivity leg for free. Decile table byte-identical (never touched the sim) => ranking kill stands. 
STALENESS RESOLVED for this experiment (verified): earnings_strategy.py imports nothing from strategy_sim/validation/significance — it computes close-to-close inline (:160-166), so of PR #28's 4 fixes only cost single-sourcing touches this path and it's now fixed. PC should still pull main for the dip book / ML scorer. 
⚠️ READ HONESTLY: SPY did ~13% CAGR 2010-2026, so headline return TIES the index — the real claim is risk-adjusted (Sharpe 1.47 vs ~0.85, maxDD 13.7% vs SPY's ~34% in 2020). Quote alpha vs SPY, never the raw 13.2% ([[calibration-counts-everything]]). And 35% avg invested = 65% IDLE — that's why the drawdown is half the index's, but it's also the strongest argument yet for a combined book. 
FRACTIONAL CLARIFIED: it's OUR policy not Alpaca's — risk_engine.py:221 blocks fractional unless intent.rebalance=True (set only at momentum.py:498,585). momentum runs in strat2 => the founder holds fractional there right now. The 'fractional shares not supported' string is misleading: it IS supported, just not permitted for that caller.

★ ROUND 3 2026-07-16 — three results, one strategic: (1) COVID GATE PASSES: 11 distinct >=5% DD episodes across 6 macro events (2011/2015-16/2018Q4/2020/2022 x2/Apr-2025); Covid deepest at 13.2% but 2022=12.4% and 2018=12.2% right behind. Ex-2020 breadth maxDD 13.2->12.4 vs concentrated 18.0->14.2 — breadth STILL wins ex-Covid. Not an artifact. (2) REBALANCING DEAD — killed by the CONTROL, not churn (churn was only ~0.9% CAGR/yr). Fixed 50x10% no-rebalance = 20.4%/21.1% vs the rebalance rule after churn = 20.0%/21.9%. The whole apparent advantage was a DEPLOYMENT effect, not a rebalancing effect. Keep the fixed fraction. (3) ★★ DEPLOYMENT IS SIGNAL-LIMITED: avg concurrent ~10; even take-everything-equal-weight-to-95% only averages 53% deployed. **95% deployment requires MORE UNCORRELATED SLEEVES, not a clever rule.** The idle 65% is NOT a bug to engineer away — it's a slot marked 'another sleeve goes here'. Confirms the combined book FROM DATA. Reframes the roadmap: the next win is a sleeve that fires when this one is QUIET (turn_of_month, residual_momentum), not more tuning. 
⚠️⚠️ THE LEVELS ARE FICTION, ONLY RANKINGS ARE VALID: linear accrual marks open trades as a straight ramp => suppresses daily vol => INFLATES Sharpe and SHALLOWS every trough (real maxDD WILL exceed these); plus the builder fills at signal close while live fires intraday. A Sharpe of 3.07 (ex-2020) is NOT REAL — no equity strategy sustains that; 1.47 is fiction too. NEVER surface these to the user as calibrated ([[decision-engine-honesty-redteam]]). 
✅ DECISION: fixed fraction, 50 slots, **5%** (~13.5% CAGR / ~13.2% model DD) NOT 10% (20.4%/21.1%). Three optimisms compound the same way (linear accrual understates DD, close fills are optimistic, zero live trades). The fraction can be raised any day after a measured season; a 30% live drawdown can't be un-lived. What kills this product is the founder losing trust, not a bad quarter. ARM WITH: notional_pct=5, max_concurrent_positions=50, max_deployed_usd=100000 (= equity; higher = unmodelled leverage).

⚠️ ROUND 4 2026-07-16 — THE 5% RECOMMENDATION WAS WRONG. Founder challenged both agents; he won. REVISED: **10 slots x 10%** (notional_pct=10, max_concurrent=10, max_deployed=100000). 
What was wrong: (a) the orchestrator's '~37% DD at 95% deployed' was FABRICATED — extrapolated linearly, never measured; the scenario CANNOT HAPPEN (deployment is signal-limited, tops out ~20% CAGR / ~22% DD). (b) 'scales proportionally, Sharpe untouched' FALSE: measured 35%->53% deployment scaled CAGR 1.46x but DD 1.66x and Sharpe FELL — because **drawdowns happen when the book is FULL** (earnings clusters coincide with market stress). Sizing is about WORST-MOMENT deployment, not average. (c) The reflex: models pattern-match to 'recommend the lower-drawdown option' because it sounds responsible. ⚠️ For capital the founder won't touch with no withdrawals, **maxDD is a PSYCHOLOGICAL statistic, not an economic one** — 50x5% is a comfort purchase costing ~7% CAGR/yr compounding (~$758k vs ~$1.86M over the window). 10% is the GROWTH-OPTIMAL point (CAGR peaks there); above it you lose return AND add DD. 20.4%/21.1% DOMINATES SPY on both axes (~20% vs 13% CAGR, ~21% vs 34% DD). 
★ THE ONE SURVIVING ARGUMENT IS DETECTION, NOT COMFORT: the deeper your NORMAL drawdown, the harder it is to detect a DEAD EDGE (at 5% a 20% DD screams; at 10% it's a Tuesday, so you'd sit through it and find out much deeper in). FIX = a PRE-REGISTERED KILL LINE decided NOW while flat, not smaller sizing. 
✅ KILL LINE: halt entries at **strat1 equity -30% from peak** (~1.5x the 21.1% model DD, which is known-optimistic); open positions run their 9d clock out; re-enable ONLY after re-validating on current data vs the original gate (never a permanent eyeballed kill). ★ MEASURABLE TODAY, NO NEW WORK — the founder is running earnings_drift ALONE in strat1, so the ACCOUNT equity curve IS the strategy P&L (account_snapshots.portfolio_value). The [[per-strategy-attribution]] gap stops blocking the moment the account is solo. Better line once auto-entries journal: realized per-trade mean vs the validated CI [+0.43,+1.28] = edge-death detection; ~100 live trades/season = a real Wilson bound. 
⚠️ Honest expectation: real maxDD WILL exceed 21.1% (linear accrual + close fills both optimistic, same direction). Budget for worse. || CLOSED 07-22 board-hygiene pass: SETTLED (memory + BUILD_LOG) — 10 slots x 10% + pre-registered -30% kill line; rebalancing + blowout-ranking DEAD; deployment signal-limited -> combined book.

cards.title: alert_style is never read — the Settings per_trade/summary control does nothing
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-16 while capping earnings_drift. `strategies.alert_style` is validated (_VALID_ALERT_STYLES = {per_trade, summary}, db/strategies.py:108), migrated in as a column (:150), stored, returned by _row_to_strategy (:186), and settable via api/strategy_routes.py:131 — but **it is never READ by any push/alert code**. grep across signals/ trading/ api/ ai/ returns zero consumers outside db/ and the write route. 
Consequences: (1) momentum_sp500's alert_style='summary' does NOTHING — momentum.py hardcodes its own notify() calls (signals/momentum.py:420,551,623), so whatever batching it does is baked into that code path, not driven by the flag; (2) the Settings UI offers a control that silently has no effect — an honesty problem (we show a knob that isn't wired); (3) setting 'summary' on any tactical strategy to tame push volume will appear to work and won't. 
Why it matters beyond cosmetics: [[auto-entry-alert-batching]] records that batching fills into ONE summary push is a MISSION-RISK item (40+/hr = alert fatigue = the founder stops trusting the agent). That memory says 'build at promotion, not now' — the point here is narrower: the column implies the feature already exists. 
FOUNDER DECISION: (a) implement it — make the auto-entry push path read alert_style and batch a scan's fills into one summary; (b) hide the control until it's real; or (c) leave it and accept the knob is decorative. Not urgent while caps keep push counts low (earnings_drift now caps at 5). 
✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-24 -- RIPPED OUT (founder chose 'remove the dead plumbing', sharpened). Key finding that reframed the card: the honesty problem it led with ('the Settings UI offers a control that does nothing') had ALREADY self-resolved -- the alert_style control died with the legacy sidebar UI (07-18); today's workspace settings-strategies-panel never renders it, nor does mobile. What remained was pure dead plumbing: a validated/stored/typed column no push code reads, and the one strategy that DOES batch (momentum) hardcodes it WITHOUT the column -- proof the column was never the right lever. Removed across db/strategies.py (const, migration ADD COLUMN, _row_to_strategy read, both SELECTs, update_strategy param+validation+setter, 3 seed UPDATE clauses -> kept entry_mode='auto'), api/strategy_routes.py (route param), frontend Strategy/StrategyPatch/LabStrategy + mobile Strategy type fields, and the 2 API + 3 DB test assertions (migration test repurposed to last_rebalanced_month). Physical prod column left dormant (harmless/unread; optional future DROP). ruff clean, 36 strategy tests green (exit 0), frontend tsc clean. FOUNDER GUARDRAIL surfaced this round + banked in [[auto-entry-alert-batching]]: batching is for post-fill REPORTS on auto strategies only -- NEVER batch the approve/reject proposal path (approvals stay per-trade so one bad pick out of many can be vetoed). A future bulk book's summary push gets built against the book's real shape, not by resurrecting this column.

cards.title: earnings_drift blindness FIXED — SEC EDGAR past announce dates (free/keyless) + Schwab severed
cards.notes:
2026-07-16: earnings_drift enabled since 06-22 and had NEVER opened a position — a real bug, not a calm tape. is_earnings_drift_entry needs a PAST earnings date to score the blowout (research/strategy_features.py:327); the calendar held only 75 past rows / 68 of 506 symbols, so 450/503 were excluded outright. Root cause traced to the 06-24 architecture decision that recorded 'past earnings date -> Finnhub' as settled WITHOUT testing it: Finnhub free /calendar/earnings serves a rolling ~30-day window (a 2-year range returns 0 rows), so the strategy was structurally blind from day one. It stayed invisible for 3 weeks because 'never triggered' is indistinguishable from 'no setup found'. signals/finnhub.py:116 afetch_past_earnings_dates is dead code — can only ever return []. 

★ FOUNDER DIRECTION: don't depend on Schwab data — it would force future users to hold a Schwab account. Capabilities must not be gated on the founder's personal setup. Reversed two earlier candidate fixes (AlphaVantage: unimplemented + 25 req/day; Schwab: works but gates the feature). 

✅ SHIPPED: signals/earnings_edgar.py — SEC EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 (Results of Operations = the legally-required earnings release, so its acceptance timestamp IS the announcement). Free, keyless, no account. Reuses the proven CIK helpers in research/fundamentals.py rather than duplicating them (signals->research imports are an established pattern). Wired into signals/earnings_refresh.py as the PAST-date source, running last so its authoritative (date,hour) wins the upsert; AV keeps the FORWARD calendar (EDGAR can't have it — an 8-K is filed after the fact, and the strategy needs both). Removed the API-key gate on arefresh: EDGAR needs no key, so past dates always refresh. 
BONUS Schwab cannot do: bmo/amc free from acceptanceDateTime, filling the `hour` column. 
SEVERED SCHWAB: api/main.py dropped the `or eq.get('last_earnings_date')` fallback; removed the now-orphaned lastEarningsDate parse from brokers/schwab_market_data.py + its key from hybrid_market_data._SCHWAB_SUPPLEMENT_KEYS (orphaned BY this change, so in scope to remove). 
Also fixed db/earnings_calendar.py:60 hardcoding source='finnhub' (mislabelled every row incl. AV's) -> per-row source, updated on conflict. And hour is now COALESCE(excluded.hour, existing) — plain excluded.hour would let an hour-less source WIPE a known bmo/amc. 

VERIFIED LIVE (not just green tests): real fetch returns AAPL 2026-04-30 amc, MSFT 04-29 amc, NVDA 05-20 amc, JPM 07-14 BMO, WMT 05-21 BMO — every ground-truth case, matching Schwab where they overlap and FRESHER (had JPM 07-14 where Schwab still showed 04-14). End-to-end into a temp DB over a 40-name S&P slice: 320 rows, **40/40 symbols now have a past date vs 68/506 in prod**, 8 quarters each (~2y), hour populated, source='edgar', COALESCE guard confirmed. 278 passed (exit 0) across watchlist/earnings/schwab/hybrid/fundamental/perception/strategy_kinds; ruff clean repo-wide. 

⚠️ KNOWN GAPS (fail-closed, logged, not silent): (1) TICKER->CIK REORG DRIFT — company_tickers.json maps to the CURRENT registrant, so XOM -> CIK 2115436 'ExxonMobil Holdings Corp' (new holdco, filings start 2026-07-01, ZERO earnings 8-Ks, formerNames EMPTY = no breadcrumb) while the 26-quarter archive sits under predecessor CIK 34088. XOM returns no dates until the holdco files its next 8-K (live self-heals); a BACKTEST would need predecessor resolution. Deliberately NOT built — logged instead. (2) ETFs (SPY) never file an 8-K -> no dates, correct. (3) Live uses filings.recent only (1 req/symbol, ~65s for 503, daily); deep history needs the filings.files[] shards — research/earnings.py already walks those for backtests. 

NEXT: deploy + confirm the first refresh populates past dates for the live universe, then watch whether earnings_drift fires in the 07-17..07-31 window (314 S&P names report; only 8 were evaluable before). ⚠️ it is entry_mode=auto on acct_alpaca_strat1 — it can now actually trade. PRE-EXISTING, flagged not fixed: _MAX_CHUNK_DAYS=30 still busts Finnhub's 1500-row cap in season and DEFAULT_DAYS_BACK=120 is fiction vs a 30d horizon (both now moot for past dates); alphavantage.py:63 throttle guard passes a comma-split 'Information' string as CSV; _fetch_quotes_sync treats Schwab's ERRORS key as a symbol.

★★ PRE-DEPLOY SIMULATION 2026-07-16 — the fix is a BIGGER behavioural change than expected. Ran the real predicate over the real sp500 with EDGAR dates + live Alpaca bars (read-only, no orders): **EVALUABLE 483/503 (was ~8), 111 had a >=5% blowout last earnings, and 51 WOULD FIRE ON THE FIRST SCAN**. earnings_drift was entry_mode=auto with NO caps (max_concurrent_positions=None, max_deployed_usd=None) x $10k notional = **$510,000 in one scan + 51 phone pushes**. It was only safe uncapped BECAUSE it was blind — fixing its vision turns it loose. Siblings were capped (steepyc_dip $20k, vix_spike $10k); earnings_drift and dip_refined were not. 
FOUNDER CALL 2026-07-16: cap it, keep auto. APPLIED to the live row (caps are enforced at strategy_scan.py:471/480, both `break` the loop): **max_concurrent_positions=5, max_deployed_usd=50000** (5 x $10k — both caps agree). Applied BEFORE deploy, which is safe in either order since the strategy is still blind until the code ships. 
⚠️ alert_style deliberately LEFT at per_trade — 'summary' is a no-op, see [alert-style-dead-column]. At a cap of 5 that's 5 pushes, not 51. 
⚠️ dip_refined is ALSO uncapped auto ($10k, no caps) — harmless today (its market-wide gate has opened 1 of 17 days) but it's the same latent shape. Founder decision, not carded separately.

★ ROUND 5 2026-07-16 — bmo/amc: we CAN tell, we CANNOT use it to shorten the exit. exit_lead_td=1 exists only because we couldn't tell the session; EDGAR's acceptanceDateTime gives one, so AMC reporters (45% of events) could in theory hold ONE EXTRA DAY = ~+11% drift on a 9-day hold. MEASURED vs Finnhub's hour on 64 shared events: 92% agree — BUT **every error is directional**: EDGAR reports the session LATER than truth, never earlier (bmo->amc x2, amc->dmh x2, bmo->dmh x1). Structural: **you cannot file an 8-K before you release**, so acceptanceDateTime is a LOWER BOUND on lateness and filing lag turns a BMO release into a fake 'amc'. ⇒ EDGAR's hour is trustworthy only in the BMO direction (where we gain nothing) and **7% wrong in the AMC direction** (2 of 28) — and a false AMC means HOLDING THROUGH THE PRINT, the exact fat-tailed event exit_lead_td=1 exists to prevent. Compounds: the FORWARD session is what an exit needs and EDGAR can't know it (no 8-K yet); inferring from history is only 78% consistent (ABBV 4amc/4bmo, AMP 4/4 = coin flips) x 93% => ~73% confidence on a fat tail. ✅ exit_lead_td=1 STAYS — the founder's original reasoning holds. The hour is still worth having: it fills the 40% of rows where Finnhub gives no hour, and it's fine for display. ⛔ Never use it to shorten the exit lead without a source of the ANNOUNCEMENT time (not filing time) for the FORWARD event.

🚀 MERGED + DEPLOYED + ARMED 2026-07-16 ~00:40 ET. PR #86 -> main 666fbe3 (CI green: lint-and-test 9m9s, frontend-typecheck 44s). Frontend rebuilt, all 4 hmt-* units restarted, ZERO tracebacks. 
★ THE BLINDNESS IS GONE — first live EDGAR refresh: 'EDGAR earnings: 3955 dates across 518 symbols' (only 18 yielded nothing = the known unmapped/reorg gap); calendar refreshed 6204 in window -> 4040 upserted. **PAST dates now 3980 rows / 501 of 503 symbols (was 75 rows / 68 symbols)**, range 2024-02-26..2026-10-14. Sources: edgar 3949 / finnhub 988. Future-row hour coverage: 297 bmo / 247 amc / 413 null => 247 events eligible for the AMC extra-day exit. 
⏱️ TIMING NOTE for future ops: the EDGAR sweep is ~2 min for 518 symbols (~0.13s throttle + ~0.5-0.7s SEC round-trip each), NOT the ~65s I estimated from the throttle alone. It runs on boot and then every 24h. The strategy stays blind until it completes. 
✅ ARMED (live row): enabled=1, entry_mode=auto, **exit_mode=auto**, notional_pct=10.0, max_concurrent_positions=10, max_deployed_usd=100000, universe=sp500, account=acct_alpaca_strat1. 
⚠️ exit_mode WAS 'propose' — changed to auto, and this was load-bearing: propose exits await phone approval, which collides with a 15-min bmo window and an after-close amc exit => a missed tap = riding THROUGH the print. It was also inverted (auto to buy $10k, permission to sell). Every other auto-entry strategy is auto/auto; every propose-exit belonged to a DISABLED strategy. Seed residue that never mattered while the sleeve was blind. 
★ FOUNDER turned the other strategies OFF — only earnings_drift (strat1) + momentum_sp500 (strat2) are enabled. strat1 is now exclusively earnings_drift, which kills the account-wide _open_exposure cap contention AND makes the kill line measurable: **strat1's equity curve IS this strategy's P&L** (no per-strategy attribution needed). 
📉 PRE-REGISTERED KILL LINE (decided while flat): halt entries if strat1 equity is -30% from peak (~1.5x the 21.1% model maxDD, which is known-optimistic — linear accrual + close fills). Open positions run their clock out; re-enable ONLY after re-validating vs the original gate.

cards.title: Equity tape collector — market-wide wildcard stream (trades+quotes), sweeps/velocity detection, local proxy for the hub

cards.title: Overnight quote showed -10% on a stock that closed +11% — boats feed served a 20.6h-old ghost print as live
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-14 20:14 ET from a founder question about NTSK. Chart + watchlist showed NTSK 12.78 / -10.44% while the stock had CLOSED 14.27, +11% on the day (real post-market print 14.4448 @ 19:52 ET, bid 14.41/ask 14.45 — a healthy book, not a liquidity vacuum). ROOT CAUSE: past 20:00 ET market_session()=='overnight' so HybridMarketData.aget_quotes routes equity ext-quotes to Alpaca's Blue Ocean overnight feed (boats). NTSK has no overnight market, and the snapshot serves the last trade it EVER saw — a 100-share print from the PRIOR overnight session (07-13 23:35 ET, 20.6h stale, superseded by a whole +11% regular session). _parse_ext_quote_snapshot read latestTrade.p and NEVER looked at latestTrade.t: no staleness guard anywhere on that path. The -10.44% is then computed correctly FROM the bad price. Gap in the shipped 'overnight-24-5-boats' card. Same family as the scars already in schwab_market_data.py (stale `extended` block / echo-close phantom prices) — and ext_price feeds PRICE ALERTS (_poll_ext_quotes_for_alerts), so a ghost price is a phantom-alert source too. FIX: trading/market_hours.last_session_close(now) + not_before guard in _parse_ext_quote_snapshot / aget_ext_quotes; drop any ext quote whose last trade predates the last regular close, and generalize hybrid's existing all-or-nothing fallback to PER-SYMBOL (a mixed watchlist has some names trading overnight and some not). VERIFIED LIVE: ext_last 12.78 -> 14.4448, ext_change_pct -10.44 -> +1.22. Tests pin the exact NTSK payload + DST/weekend edges. FOLLOW-UP: hybrid's broad `except Exception` swallowed a TypeError from the new kwarg — it hides signature errors; worth narrowing.

2026-07-19 board review: CLOSED — verified live (ext_last 12.78→14.4448, ext_change_pct −10.44→+1.22); per-symbol fallback shipped. Minor follow-up stays here: hybrid's broad `except Exception` swallows signature errors — narrow when touched next.

cards.title: Flow engine ran on 0.7% of the chain — bare snapshot = 100 alphabetical contracts, SPY/QQQ/TSLA never saw a put
cards.notes:
THE root data bug, found in the 2026-07-14 data-layer limits audit (founder: 'this is the data, without good data this app is nothing'). poll.py called adapter.get_option_chain_snapshot(u) BARE; the method defaults to limit=None/max_pages=1 = Alpaca's own page default of 100 contracts ALPHABETICAL. An OCC sorts expiry -> C before P -> strike, so one bare page = the nearest expiry, CALLS ONLY. MEASURED live 2026-07-14: SPY has 13,730 contracts / 35 expiries / 6,865 puts and we saw 100 calls at one expiry = 0.7% of the chain. 11 of 30 underlyings NEVER saw a put (AMD,CRWD,GLD,GS,KLAC,MU,NBIS,QQQ,SPCX,SPY,TSLA — it hits the MOST liquid names hardest, since more strikes means the page fills with calls before reaching P); 22 of 30 saw one expiry. IMPACT: aggregate_directional_pressure tracks call_net/put_net, so put_net was STRUCTURALLY ZERO for our three biggest names — every SPY/QQQ/TSLA directional read was bullish by construction. A signal fabricated by omission. ACTIVE_SET_PER_UNDERLYING=60 never once selected on merit; it picked 60 from a pre-truncated alphabetical 100, which is why every cap we debated was downstream of a gutted pool. ⚠️ WE ALREADY KNEW: BUILD.md 2026-07-09 records the identical diagnosis ('unfiltered snapshot pages alphabetically -> one expiry, no puts') — found and fixed in the CHAIN VIEWER only (options_chain.py: expiration_date + limit=1000 + max_pages=3, live-verified NVDA 25 expirations x 86 strikes both sides). The poll was never carried across, and the method docstring enshrined it: 'Defaults (no filter, one page) keep the original single-page behavior the poll's active-set relies on.' The UI the founder reads manually was correct; the engine meant to think for him was not. FIX: page the chain (CHAIN_SNAPSHOT_PAGE_LIMIT=1000 vendor max, CHAIN_SNAPSHOT_MAX_PAGES=20; SPY needs 14 = 1.16s, whole watchlist ~16s per 300s refresh, ~0.3% of the 10,000/min REST budget) + the pager now WARNS when it truncates instead of dropping the tail silently. VERIFIED against the LIVE chain: active set = 1000 contracts, 395 puts / 605 calls, 30 underlyings, 29 distinct expiries; SPY now 20 puts / 16 calls (was 0 puts). 196 tests green, ruff clean. New test is a true behavioural repro (old code fails: 'one page IS the vendor's alphabetical default — no puts'). CONSEQUENCE FLAGGED: ~1,800 contracts now rank active vs the 1,000 sub budget, so STREAM_TRADES_MAX binds HARD for the first time (~33-36 per underlying). Vendor acked 1,506 and the client has ~150x headroom, so 1000->1500 is probably free — unverified; a 405 would now surface via PR #72's error-frame logging. See References/DATA_LAYER_LIMITS_AUDIT_2026-07-14.md. Land AFTER the close (multiplies the candidate pool ~50x; not a market-hours change). DEPLOYED 2026-07-14 20:01 UTC — after the close, as this card required (merged d7d5104, PR #75). Re-verified ON THE DEPLOYED TREE through the production get_broker('alpaca') path: SPY 13,730 contracts / 6,865 puts / 35 expiries; TSLA 5,709 / 2,855 puts / 23 expiries (was 100 calls, one expiry, zero puts). Post-close the stream reports trade_subs=0, which is CORRECT (the subscription set is empty outside the regular session) — so the put_net-is-no-longer-zero verification needs the 13:30 UTC open. Card stays in_progress: deployed != verified.

2026-07-19 board review: CLOSED — fix deployed + re-verified through the production path (SPY 13,730 contracts / 6,865 puts). The outstanding put_net-at-open verify is answered by live evidence: the gauge measured SPX bear PREMIUM (puts) through real opens 07-16/17.

cards.title: Options-flow pipeline extracted to its own process (hmt-flow-collector)
cards.notes: Motivated by the OPEN 2026-07-13 backend loop-stall incident (20-30s asyncio stalls killed both streams; in-process OPRA collector = suspect): a stalled API loop blinds the stream, a hot open can starve the trading loops. The glue (intraday poll + sweep consumer + stream owner, previously UNTESTED in the api/main.py god-file) moved verbatim to signals/options_flow/runner.py; both hosts share it — API in-process (legacy default, unchanged) or tools/flow_collector.py standalone. Interlock: OPTIONS_FLOW_EXTERNAL_COLLECTOR=1 in the shared .env flips ownership atomically (API refuses to start it in-process, collector refuses to start without it — never two OPRA sockets, Alpaca 406s the second). Cross-process bridge = data/trading.db (WAL already on every connection). Collector re-reads settings each poll tick (new config.settings.reload_settings) so watchlist edits in the API propagate without restart. serv-deploy.sh restarts the collector with backend deploys when the unit exists. 8 new tests pin the seams (first coverage this glue has ever had); 405 api.main-importing + flow tests green, ruff clean. SEQUENCING: do NOT deploy before the 2026-07-15 open verifies PRs #71-#76 on the current single-process architecture (one variable at a time). FOUNDER: one-time sudo to install the unit — see SERVER_SETUP.md 'hmt-flow-collector' (flip .env flag + enable unit + backend restart; rollback = reverse both). VERIFIED 2026-07-16 at the open: pre-open warm delivered trade_subs=1000 by 13:24Z (6 min early), reconnects=0, rotation cycling through the burst; classified 59.0% (270/458) vs 46.2/21.5 baselines; burst lag upstream-only (p95 10.1s→208ms in 2 min, client idle). DONE.

cards.title: Flow watcher never watched SPY/TSLA — FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-14 (0 → 16 TSLA events in 3 min)
cards.notes: Found chasing the STREAM_TRADES_MAX alphabetical clip (flow-open-blindness follow-up); the clip turned out to be the SMALL half. MEASURED against the live chain 2026-07-14 16:31 UTC: _all_watchlist_symbols() returns sorted(set(...)) and both options_flow paths then did [:OPTIONS_FLOW_MAX_UNDERLYINGS] — i.e. underlyings were selected ALPHABETICALLY. With 33 watchlist symbols and a cap of 25, that silently evicted SHAZ,SLB,SLV,SPCX,SPY,TSLA,XLE,XLF: **SPY and TSLA — the two biggest options-flow names there are — were never watched at all**, intraday OR nightly (scan.py had the same line). Worse, 3 of the 25 slots were burned on futures roots (/CL,/ES,/NQ) which 400 on Alpaca's options endpoints and sort FIRST on the leading '/', so they were guaranteed to waste a slot + a REST call every cycle. FIX: shared scan.eligible_underlyings() (futures filtered, over-cap = loud WARNING naming the dropped tickers instead of a silent slice) used by both scan.py and poll.py; cap 25→30 so the real watchlist fits (30 eligible = 30). Contract level: _refresh_active_set now allocates the STREAM_TRADES_MAX budget ROUND-ROBIN by rank across underlyings — every underlying's #1 before any underlying's #2 — so a busy name can't crowd out a quiet one and nothing dies by spelling; shallow underlyings use less than their share and the deep ones keep the surplus. Over-budget is logged. VERIFIED live: newly covered = SHAZ,SLB,SLV,SPCX,SPY,TSLA,XLE,XLF; futures no longer requested; zero underlyings with no coverage. 179 options_flow tests green, ruff clean. TRADE-OFF (flagged): deep names (AAPL/NVDA/QQQ) now share the 1,000-sub budget with 30 underlyings instead of 22, so their per-name depth drops from up to 60. Worth it — covering SPY/TSLA at depth ~33-50 beats covering NVDA at 60 and SPY at 0. FOLLOW-UP: constants.py says the vendor acked 1,500+ trade subs and the 2026-07-14 probe proved the client has ~150x headroom, so raising STREAM_TRADES_MAX 1000→1500 is likely free — but unverified; a 405 'symbol limit exceeded' would now surface via PR #72's error-frame logging. DEPLOYED 2026-07-14 16:47 UTC (main 20e5ea8, MainPID 2153012; clean restart, no 406, lag p50=13ms). VERIFIED LIVE from options_flow_events, before vs after: BEFORE (14:00-16:47, old code, 2h45m) SPY=0 TSLA=0 SLV=0 XLE=0 XLF=0 SPCX=0 — all six evicted names produced ZERO events; AFTER (16:47:45+, ~3 min) TSLA=16 SPCX=6 SLV=3 SPY=1 XLE=1 XLF=1. TSLA went 0-in-2h45m -> 16-in-3min. The round-robin log fires as designed and loud: 'options_flow poll: 1448 ranked contracts over the 1000 sub budget — allocating round-robin across 30 underlyings (~33 each)'. (An earlier read of 'TSLA=326 last hour' that seemed to contradict the diagnosis was MY query bug: created_at is an ISO string, so max(created_at)-3600000 coerced to a number and matched every row — it was an all-time count. Don't re-litigate; the before/after above is the real measurement.)

cards.title: Flow watcher was blind through the open (trade_subs=0 at the bell) — OI seed + open-aware resubscribe
cards.notes:
Found while reading the 2026-07-14 open probe. Prod's OPRA stream carried ZERO trade subscriptions through the bell — confirmed with no probe interference on 7/10: msgs=0 / trade_subs=0 at 13:30:21, 13:31:22, 13:32:22, first data only 13:33:22. We were missing the first ~2-3 min of every session, the most informative flow window, BY ACCIDENT. Two stacked causes: (a) signals/options_flow/poll.py _refresh_active_set ranks contracts by latestTrade 'today', which at the bell is empty BY CONSTRUCTION (state.oi was never wired to seed membership, only to enrich); (b) signals/options_flow/stream.py SUB_REFRESH_SECONDS=300 is anchored to CONNECT time, not the market clock — the only forced refresh is at connect (~15 min pre-open, session='pre' => empty set), so the first post-open re-check landed 0-5 min late, drifting daily. FIX (this PR): seed the active set from prior-session OI when the today-trade ranking is empty (_refresh_oi already runs first on the opening tick, so no market-hours gate change needed), and force a resubscribe the moment the set turns non-empty instead of waiting out the 5-min grid. Seed is sized to STREAM_TRADES_MAX/underlyings — the whole watchlist seeds at once (25x60=1,500 > the 1,000 budget) and _desired_trades() clips ALPHABETICALLY, which would have silently dropped whole underlyings from the back of the alphabet. 4 new tests: 2 are true old-bug repros verified to fail on the old code with the exact production symptom (active set is literally set() at the bell; 'stream stayed unsubscribed after the active set filled'). The other 2 are guards, not repros — the budget-cap test pins a failure mode THIS change introduces (against old code it errors on the monkeypatch, not behaviourally, since there is no seed to overflow), and the prefers-today-trades test passes on old code by construction (guards the new seed from shadowing live prints). ruff + 174 options_flow tests green. VERIFY AT THE NEXT OPEN: trade_subs>0 in the 13:30 stats line, and prod's own lag_p50/p95 across 13:30-13:32 settles branch W vs C for free (see flow-wildcard-probe). NOT covered: being live at 13:30:00.000 still needs a pre-open warmup path (the poll job's market-hours gate + a ~30s tick + a 25-underlying REST chain walk); deferred — the window it recovers is the one where Alpaca's feed is 3-6s stale anyway. DEPLOYED 2026-07-14 16:20 UTC (PR #71, 884fa29). Card stays in_progress: merged+deployed != verified — the bell verify (trade_subs>0 in the 13:30 stats line, plus lag_p50/p95 across 13:30-13:32 settling branch W vs C) happens at the 2026-07-15 open.

2026-07-15 bell verify: still blind ~50s (13:30:00->13:30:50) — the RTH gate held the OI seed hostage; the seed itself worked (fired 20s into the poll). Fix shipped in flow quote rotation v2 (pre-open warm window).

cards.title: Flow stream: reconcile subscriptions against server acks (silent-blindness alarm)
cards.notes:
Follow-up hardening from the PR #71 review (flow-open-blindness): the deepest lesson of the open-blindness bug is that the stream sat silently unsubscribed for weeks because it ignores Alpaca's 'subscription' echo and post-handshake 'error' frames — _subscribed_trades is optimistic (assumes every subscribe succeeded). This PR is LOG-ONLY: parse the subscription echo into a server-confirmed set, add ack_trades/ack_quotes to the minute stats line, WARN when confirmed trade subs persistently diverge from client state (10s settle grace so a refresh's own echoes land first; quote subs excluded from the alarm — they churn via hot-quote adds), and WARN on any server error frame. Converts the whole silent-blindness failure class into a <=1min visible alarm; wins in both branch-W and branch-C worlds. Verified: 3 new tests (divergence warns / matching ack doesn't / error frame logged) + ScriptWS upgraded to echo FULL server state like the real feed; 16 stream tests green; replay bench on the real 7/14 open tape unchanged (149k msgs/s — hot path untouched). ⚠ SEQUENCING: deploy AFTER tomorrow's open verifies PR #71 — the bell experiment must run on exactly the reviewed code. DEPLOYED 2026-07-14 16:20 UTC (PR #72, d0ab85c). ⚠ DEVIATION, recorded honestly: this card said 'deploy AFTER tomorrow's open verifies PR #71 — the bell experiment must run on exactly the reviewed code.' That did NOT happen; it shipped alongside PR #71. Judged harmless and net-POSITIVE rather than reverted: the change is log-only with the hot path untouched (its own replay bench on the real 7/14 open tape: 149k msgs/s unchanged), so it cannot alter subscription behaviour, and ack_trades/ack_quotes make the 7/15 bell verify STRONGER — server-confirmed sub counts instead of optimistic client state. Flagging so the card does not claim a sequencing that was not followed.

2026-07-19 board review: shipped alongside #71 (log-only, server-ack-confirmed sub counts); has served every live bell verify since.

2026-07-14 — POST-CLOSE GRADING BUG (fixed, same round as overnight-ext-quote-stale). NTSK was marked `lost` FOUR MINUTES after it was created. The nightly scan ran 17:44 ET on a +11% breakout day (open 12.48 / low 12.40 / close 14.27) and proposed the 14.23-14.37 zone, stop 13.59. The sweep then replayed that SAME already-complete bar, saw the 12.40 MORNING low under the stop, and stopped the idea out — on price action from hours BEFORE the breakout the idea was built on. _process_pending skipped only `bar_date < as_of_date`, and as_of_date was the UTC date of a post-close timestamp, so the birth-day bar always counted. EVERY real idea is minted post-close (scans run after the bell), so this contaminates the whole calibration ledger — it fabricates LOSSES, deflating win%. FIX: _first_evaluable_date() — an idea minted after the close is graded from the NEXT trading day (bar filter + fetch bound + TTL basis). Intraday ideas unaffected (existing tests all still pass). DATA REPAIR STILL OWED: idea_outcomes rows id=8 and id=10 (both NTSK, artifacts 183/184) are fabricated losses — reset to pending or discard before they reach win%. ALSO SEEN: 183/184 are DUPLICATE NTSK ideas (same plan, two artifacts ~19min apart) — the scan re-proposed an identical idea; worth its own look.

cards.notes: ANSWERED by the 2026-07-14 automated open probe (13:29:20 UTC, 180s across the bell; research/options_flow/rate_probe_2026-07-14_1329.log + data/tape_2026-07-14_1329_open.mpk). Importance scoring should be unusualness-vs-per-name-baseline weighted by tenor/moneyness + event proximity (EDGAR dates), never absolute notional floors. Flow-lane ideas grade at short horizons.\n\n[2026-07-26 audit round] (!) CORRECTS THE PREMISE OF THIS CARD. 'Pushes are dead' is WRONG -- measured 75 'Sent alert push' lines in 3 days of hmt-backend journal: idea-triggered, price alerts, the Idea Engine canary, and all three LLM books all reached the phone on 07-24. Only the convergence/solo FLOW rows are dead (the 07-21/22 founder order), and only those were ever budget-gated. Reason the budget looks irrelevant: _notify_idea_transition (api/main.py:721-761) calls notify(push=True) -> signals/notify.py:99-115 -> send_alert_push DIRECTLY, never touching signals/push_budget.py. So alerts.max_push_per_day=0 gates ONE lane, not the phone. Two consequences found the same round: (a) 12 idea-trigger pushes fired inside ONE SECOND on 07-24 -- un-batched, the exact 'first-5-of-hundreds' failure the flow lane was killed over, arriving through a different door (see auto-entry-alert-batching: batching is for REPORTS, never approvals); (b) the backend logs 'APNs is in SANDBOX mode', so a TestFlight/App Store build would receive NOTHING. cards.title: Frontend poll hygiene: CORS preflight storm + duplicate/hidden-page pollers
cards.notes: Root pricehistory flood FIXED earlier (per-(symbol,timeframe) TTL cache + SIP-hybrid moved equities off Schwab). || 07-25 RESEARCH: card confirmed and it UNDERSTATED the problem. Measured on live serv: /api/price-alerts 1,255 GET/2h (one per 5.7s) with OPTIONS 1:1, and 48.6% of ALL backend requests were CORS preflights carrying no data (5,150/10,596 in 2h; peak 10,776 req/hr = 3 req/s). ROOT CAUSE (measured in clean headless Chromium against the real :4443->:8443 origins, not inferred): `cache: "no-store"` makes Chromium BYPASS its CORS preflight cache - 6 preflights per 6 fetches vs 1 on the default cache mode. apiFetch sends X-API-Token on every call (non-simple -> preflight) and 72 call sites passed no-store. Server was innocent: Access-Control-Max-Age reached the browser intact through tailscale serve. || PHASE 1 SHIPPED + DEPLOYED 07-25: no-store moved request->response (SecurityMiddleware setdefault so ai_routes SSE keeps its own no-cache), apiFetch pins cache:"default", CORS max_age 600->86400. Verified live: preflight share 48.6% -> 14.2%. || PHASE 2/3 SHIPPED + DEPLOYED 07-25: new usePagePoll hook (lib/workspace/use-page-poll.ts) pauses the INTERVAL on hidden workspace pages and refreshes on show; ALL 6 pages stay mounted (founder 07-25: instant Alt+1/2/3 is deliberate, do NOT unmount) and the FIRST load deliberately ignores visibility so a hidden page still holds data. 11 widgets migrated; options-chain/scans/watchlist/native-chart/use-watchlist-market gated directly (they have no immediate-fetch semantics to preserve, or would refetch on hide). cards.title: Memory P3 lifecycle: valid_until now ENFORCED — an expired thesis no longer injects as current fact
cards.notes:
The last open thread from memory-overhaul. valid_until was stored on every memory row but NEVER enforced — a thesis past its date kept ranking into the propose-order-capable chat prompt as current fact. FIX (db/ai_tables.py + ai/memories/retrieval.py + ai/chat/context.py): (1) expire_stale_memories() — the SOLE writer of status='expired' — parses each active row's free-form valid_until defensively (_parse_valid_until: date-only = valid through end of that day; ISO datetime; 'Z'/offset; naive→UTC; garbage→None→left active, non-destructive) and flips past-due rows; every read path already filters status='active', so an expired row drops everywhere at once. (2) The sweep runs at the top of retrieve_relevant_memories (ALL injection paths funnel through it), fail-soft — a sweep error degrades to 'nothing expired this turn', never breaks retrieval. (3) Belt-and-suspenders: the injection fence turn_memory_context also drops is_memory_expired(m) in-memory, so an expired-but-still-active row (sweep write raced/failed) still can't reach the prompt. Deny-by-default on UNPARSEABLE dates = KEEP injecting (reviewer-validated: the opposite would let a prompt-injection call update_memory(<the 20% cap directive>, valid_until='garbage') SILENTLY DELETE a live risk guardrail from the prompt — strictly worse than retaining a provenance-labeled stale thesis). REVIEWED by 2 split-mandate Opus (correctness + safety/fence): both SHIP, no HIGH/MED; acted on the one flagged item (per-turn WARNING spam on a malformed date → debug). Tests +9 (parser formats, is_memory_expired, sweep flips-only-past + idempotent, e2e sweep-before-read, fence drops expired-but-active); targeted memory+chat suites green, ruff clean. Zero live risk today (memories table empty, no thesis rows). FAST-FOLLOW (both reviewers, non-blocking): surface unparseable-valid_until rows to the founder trust widget so a typo'd thesis date gets CORRECTED rather than injecting forever behind a debug line — do when the widget is next touched + thesis rows exist. 
🚀 DEPLOYED + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-24 ~09:28 ET (PR #105 -> main ceeb26f): backend restarted BACKEND-ONLY (kill MainPID -> systemd respawn; collectors 2081593/2082050 + frontend 1841841 PIDs UNCHANGED, OPRA socket + equity tape never dropped), pre-bell; /health 200 poll_healthy; clean boot (no import/memory tracebacks). Live smoke on deployed venv: parser + is_memory_expired fence guard + sweep flip + active-read exclusion + idempotency all green.

Real Decision-Engine quality work lives in decision-engine-phase1, not here.\n\n[2026-07-26 audit round] CLOSED as done. cards.title: Settings apply_settings_patch read-modify-write race can lost-update kill_switch/entries_halted
cards.notes: FIXED 2026-07-12 (branch worktree-board-knockout, draft PR). Root: apply_settings_patch did load_settings()(lock/unlock) -> re-read on-disk -> merge -> save_settings()(lock/unlock) with the lock RELEASED between read and write, so two concurrent PUTs last-writer-win and one could lost-update a breaker-armed kill_switch_active/entries_halted back to False. Fix: whole RMW now under a NEW _patch_lock (via _apply_settings_patch_locked), kept SEPARATE from _settings_lock (stays a plain brief Lock). Adversarial review (Sonnet) rejected the naive 'widen _settings_lock to RLock' first pass: an ai patch runs a synchronous model-list HTTP probe (maybe_upgrade_default_llm, ~6s x several endpoints) that under the reader lock would stall is_kill_switch_active/is_entries_halted (gate every order) for seconds; _patch_lock only serializes patch-vs-patch, never the fast readers. Deterministic regression test proven to FAIL on old code + pass on fix; 100+ settings/safety/auth/research/strategy tests green, ruff clean. Pending backend deploy.
