cards.title: Intraday position-watch — event-gated LLM wake-ups + order-management verbs (agent-awareness layer)
cards.notes: Design captured 2026-07-24 (founder discussion; not started). PROBLEM: the nightly book cycle is a script that dies overnight — nothing manages open positions intraday; exits/optimization happen only at night, and a thesis formed at 5pm executes ~16h later at a gap-risk open. GOAL = the 'agent aware of its own positions' layer, as two typed nodes on the book graph: (Aggregator) an EVENT-GATED position-watch = PERCEIVE, and (Sink) ORDER-MANAGEMENT VERBS (cancel/replace/exit through the chokepoint) = ACT. ⚠️ VERBS ARE THE PREREQUISITE — build the ability to act before the trigger to act on, or it's just a smarter pager (today: interim holds_review, founder acts manually). Absorbs the 'NEXT INCREMENT: analyst order-management verbs' item from [[llm-books-program]]; relates to stop-lifecycle-v2. ── GATING MECHANICS (the hard part, solved in discussion): do NOT gate on a static threshold — gate on decision-relevant CHANGE. (1) EDGE-trigger not level-trigger: fire on the transition INTO a danger zone and consume it, don't re-fire while the condition stays true. (2) HYSTERESIS / Schmitt trigger: arm ~1.5% from stop, disarm only after recovery past ~3% — kills the 'price hovers just above stop all day' chatter. (3) The LLM AUTHORS ITS OWN RE-ARM CONDITION each wake ('hold unless price breaks 312 OR vol >3x on a down bar OR a downgrade prints') → the cheap loop then watches THAT narrower tripwire; the gate self-sharpens per wake (the 'rejected-idea-writes-a-rule' loop applied to monitoring). (4) NEWS gated by materiality x price-confirmation: dedup/cluster (50 rewrites=1 event), primary-catalyst-class only (earnings/guidance/downgrade/M&A/SEC/FDA, not 'analyst reiterates'), AND require an abnormal price/vol move — news alone is LOGGED as position context, never a wake; price is the arbiter of whether news mattered. Solves 'headlines all day that do nothing to price' by construction. (5) HARD BUDGET CAP per position/day → on breach, batch into ONE 'X is unusually active, auto-watch paused' push to founder, never a token spend-spiral. ── SHIPPING PHILOSOPHY (founder call 07-24, 'too many things in shadow mode'): PERCEIVE+PROPOSE ships LIVE now with sane defaults + the cap (downside is cheap — tokens/notifications, bounded by cap), tune from real behavior; NO shadow-mode study. The ONLY rung that earns a measured proving period is the propose→AUTO-EXIT flip (expensive/irreversible = real money + trust; autonomy ladder). Test for shadow-mode = 'is being wrong expensive AND irreversible?' — the wake-up gate is neither. Downside is ALSO already covered intraday by resting GTC stops (broker-enforced in RTH) → the watch is OPTIMIZATION not blowup-prevention, which is why it can stay cheap + event-gated. ── RELATED (same discussion, own follow-up): make the nightly panel judge BLIND to the analyst's rhetoric/self-graded win% — re-derive its own verdict from data + the pre-registered rubric (maker-checker; the Fable judge is the MOST capable model, correct for this seat — see [[agent-model-budget-routing]]). ── SEQUENCE: (a) management verbs behind the chokepoint (adversarial review — trading/ safety), (b) event-gated watch on the existing backend poll loop in PROPOSE mode + defaults + cap, (c) tune triggers from live behavior, (d) later: propose→auto-exit after a measured track record. Graph vocabulary borrowed from the 'graph engineering' pattern (worker/validator/aggregator/sink) but NO framework migration — deprioritized plumbing per mission; use patterns we already have (Workflow harness, poll loop, cron).

cards.title: Whole-market OPRA directional-flow corpus — the 1,000-sub cap bought out for $199/mo
cards.notes:
Founder subscribed Databento Standard 2026-07-26. Verified by get_cost, not assumed: whole-market OPRA tcbbo 12mo went $36,779.72 -> $0.00; L1 window is EXACTLY 12 months and ROLLS DAILY (18mo still quotes $14,964.49), so days not archived before they age out become a purchase -- the backfill has a deadline, not just a cost. L0 (statistics/ohlcv/definition) is free to 2013, which retroactively zeroes the $51,659 full-universe OI quote BUILD_LOG 07-19 recorded as dead.
WHY IT MATTERS: our own lane resolves direction on 57.4% of events and is 41.8% BLIND in the opening 30min (anchor warm-up), across ~21 contracts on 40 names. tcbbo attaches the NBBO at print time: 89.0% of prints / 92.7% of premium classified, FLAT across the session (58.1% open vs 57.3% rest), on every contract of every name. The anchor/hot-pool/promotion tuning that was queued before this is now DEAD WORK -- do not build it.
Shipped this round: tools/opra_tcbbo_backfill.py (resumable, per-day cost guard aborts above --max-cost, default $0.00 -- the $43 overage of 07-19 had no funds pre-check), db/flow_corpus.py + tools/flow_corpus_rollup.py (11s/session on numpy; pandas rejected because serv had 6GB free while holding the OPRA socket), tools/flow_corpus_bars.py (Alpaca, recursive bisection on 400).
MEASURED, decides an open question: unserved-by-Alpaca premium is 30.8% and it is ENTIRELY index roots (SPX/SPXW/NDX/VIX/RUT) that NO equity vendor serves. Delisted equities are $11M of $45,573M = 0.02%. => the $4.82 Databento point-in-time backfill buys nothing. NOT buying.
Open: backfill completing (~260 sessions); index-root spot needs a proxy or stays 'unknown' (prereg's secondary arm excludes index roots anyway); 0.37% unresolved prints CLOSED (all instrument 5930 / BBX / class 'K' INDEX; the C/P filter is also the only thing stopping their size==UINT32_MAX from inflating a session ~9.2e8x).
Addendum B (07-26): spot-reference rule pinned — historic AND live both use the PRIOR-SESSION split-adjusted close, even live, because a reference change at the historic->live seam fabricates a change event on every underlying at once. Spot source is part of schema_version; changing it is a full re-roll (raw prints retained so it stays a re-roll, not a re-purchase). Index spot DEFERRED as a decision: Databento sells us no index dataset (29 available, none index); put-call parity from our own prints recovers SPX 7,484.30 / NDX 28,524.55 / RUT 2,942.73 but at +-0.4-1.3% crude, too loose for a 2% bucket boundary until done per-expiry and time-matched.
LIVE SWAP built 2026-07-26 (founder: 'retire a databento module so we could easily swap back' — Alpaca is NOT deleted): signals/options_flow/dbn_stream.py duck-types OptionsFlowStream's surface (collected_prints/quote_at/acked_market_wide/run/stop), reuses normalize_print so the print shape is identical, and quote_at returns the print's OWN attached NBBO — zero staleness, no quote cache, no anchors, no hot pool. Selected by settings options_flow.provider, DEFAULT 'alpaca' (ships off, armed deliberately, per strategy-off-by-default). NO auto-fallback either direction: a dead session logs loud and stops, because silently degrading to the worse source is the exact shape that left the copilot web-blind 3x. direction_basis='dbn_nbbo' stamped per print (runner.py now reads quote_basis off the print instead of hard-coding 'stream_quote') so post-swap events never pool with the Alpaca era in options_flow_events. ONE variable changes: same watchlist (parent-symbol subscribe), same detectors, same thresholds — widening to whole-market is a separate step or a regression cannot be attributed. Live entitlement probed OK (parent stype accepted, session opened/closed clean). 5 new tests; 2,784 passing.
⏳ NOT ARMED — do not flip options_flow.provider until the backfill lands and the provider is verified against a session whose ground truth we already hold.
⚠️ DEFINITION PULL WAS BROKEN — found + fixed 07-26 while recovering the crashed session. The per-date ET session window was applied to EVERY schema, including `definition`. Definitions are a START-OF-DAY SNAPSHOT, not intraday events, so any window not starting at UTC midnight returns only contracts newly listed inside it. Databento warns on this explicitly and we were ignoring it. Measured, OPRA.PILLAR ALL_SYMBOLS 2025-07-28: ET window = 0.1 MB billable / 285 records vs full UTC day = 575.4 MB / 1,598,325 records — a 5,754x under-pull, both quoted $0.00. Since ALL_SYMBOLS files ship no symbology mappings, definition is the ONLY instrument_id -> underlying/strike/expiry/right resolver: the corpus would have completed ~57 GB of prints that resolve to NOTHING, looking finished on disk the whole time. Fixed by branching the window per schema (_definition_bounds_utc vs _session_bounds_utc); re-pull of 2025-07-28 verified 285 -> 1,598,325 records, warning gone. The 8 truncated defs files were deleted so they re-pull (the skip guard is size>0, and 7 KB passes it — they would have been skipped forever).
⚠️ AND THE REVIEWERS' DST FIX HAD NEVER SHIPPED. tools/opra_tcbbo_backfill.py existed as TWO divergent copies: the one actually executed (dev/help_me_trade, UNTRACKED on main) carried the corrected ET bounds, while the TRACKED copy on this branch still had the original RTH=('T13:30','T20:00') fixed UTC slice. The live run was correct so nothing looked wrong — a silent-success one level up from the class this card keeps hitting. Both fixes are now in the tracked copy.
Resumed 07-26 19:47 via tools/opra_backfill_run.sh — setsid-detached so it survives the session, nice+ionice, defs THEN tcbbo sequentially (two concurrent ALL_SYMBOLS pulls is what helped swap the box flat). Progress: tail data/databento/run.log. At restart: tcbbo 26/260, defs 2/260.
Open: backfill completing (~260 sessions x2); tcbbo BBO semantics STILL UNSETTLED — is the attached quote the one prevailing immediately BEFORE the print? Three reviewers were killed mid-flight before answering; partial finding is that `action` surfaces as `_reserved1` (84='T') with bid_pb/ask_pb present. Re-run ONE reviewer at a time, not three concurrent Opus agents against a 258 MB file.
✅ tcbbo BBO SEMANTICS SETTLED 07-26 — the quote is PRE-TRADE. Vendor's own words, read out of the installed databento_dbn package rather than scraped: TCBBO = "consolidated best bid and offer trade record containing the consolidated BBO before the trade"; sibling TBBO = "All trade events with the best bid and offer (BBO) immediately **before** the effect of the trade" (Databento's own emphasis). Corroborated empirically on TWO sessions (tools/tcbbo_semantics_probe.py, 14.3M prints, 2025-08-26 + 2025-08-28): 62.9%/63.2% of prints sit exactly AT the touch, while only 0.38-0.51% print above the ask and 0.45-0.50% below the bid — a post-trade book would have moved away and could not concentrate mass on the touch like that. Decisive corroborator: ~26% of at-ask prints carry size >= the displayed ask size (2.4-2.6% strictly exceed it), which is contradictory under a post-trade quote — the book cannot still be showing an offer the print already consumed. Founder's 99% recollection was right.
⚠️ BUT: THE QUOTE IS ONE SNAPSHOT PER SWEEP, NOT PER LEG. 99.4% of multi-print groups sharing an (instrument_id, ts_event) carry an IDENTICAL bid/ask. So every leg of a sweep is signed against the same pre-sweep quote — correct as a direction reference, but N legs are NOT N independent quote observations, and book-walking depth cannot be inferred from the attached BBO. Any statistic that weights by print count across a sweep is double-counting one observation.
⚠️ ALSO MEASURED: the `side` field is 'N' on 100% of prints (all 14.3M) — OPRA never populates it, so direction is quote-derived by necessity, not by choice. And ~37% of prints fall STRICTLY INSIDE the spread, unsignable by the touch test; the 89.0%-classified figure must lean on a midpoint/tick rule for that third — confirm which, and how exact-mid prints are handled, before the study reads through it.
✅ THE 0.37% UNRESOLVED PRINTS ARE EXPLAINED (07-26) — close that open question. On 2025-07-28 the join drops 24,298 prints = 0.3494%, and they are ALL one instrument: instrument_id 5930, raw_symbol BBX, instrument_class 'K' (INDEX), with UNDEF strike and UNDEF expiration. _load_definitions already keeps only 'C'/'P', so class-K never enters d_ids and every one of its prints is dropped by the join. Dropping them is CORRECT — they are not options. Also note they carry size == UINT32_MAX (the DBN unset sentinel), so had they survived the join, `premium = price/PX * size * 100` would have inflated session premium ~918,000,000x ($26.3B -> $24.2 QUINTILLION). The C/P filter is the only thing preventing that: it is load-bearing and non-obvious, so do NOT relax the join to 'recover' unresolved prints without adding an explicit size-sentinel guard first.
CLASSIFIER AUDIT, post-join, the numbers the corpus actually stores (tools/flow_classifier_audit.py, 2025-07-28, 6,930,544 prints after join): side-classified = 87.83% (docstring says ~89%; buy 42.29% / sell 45.54%), at-mid-unsigned 10.06%, good_q 97.89%, unquoted 1.22%, locked 0.88%, crossed 0.01%. Strict/touch rule signs only 61.9% and leaves 36.01% inside. Premium clean at $26,310,928,243.
⛔ REAL DEFECT — u_prem's SIGN IS SET BY 0.40% OF PRINTS. `u = (price-mid)/half` is UNBOUNDED (measured range [-61, +90]) and u_prem is a premium-weighted SUM. Prints with |u|>2 are 0.40% of the corpus but contribute 171.92% of sum(u*premium): total = +366,445,672 while the |u|>2 tail alone = +629,989,228, so the other 99.6% of prints sum to -263,543,556. The aggregate reads BULLISH while the bulk of flow leans BEARISH, purely on outliers. Any 'flow leaned long/short' read off u_prem is an artifact until u is bounded (winsorize or clip to [-1,1]) or u_prem is stored alongside a robust counterpart. ⚠️ u is a PRE-REGISTERED metric — changing its definition post-hoc is a prereg violation, so this is a founder decision, NOT an agent fix.
⚠️ minor: rollup line 158 nan_to_num(u, nan=0.0) maps bad-quote prints onto u=0.0, which is exactly the value meaning 'printed at the midpoint' — 0.54% of premium is folded into at-mid rather than excluded. ⚠️ minor: rollup line 123 does to_ndarray() with NO chunking, materializing a whole session (~500MB raw + float64 copies) before the 260-session run; the audit/probe tools chunk at 1M records for this reason.
✅ u_premium_clipped SHIPPED 07-26 (SCHEMA_VERSION 1->2, ALTER-migrated; v1 rows read as not-ingested so they re-roll). The pre-registered u_premium is stored UNCHANGED; the clipped counterpart is the labelled post-hoc robustness check. Same doctrine the rollup docstring already applied to midpoint-vs-strict: write both so neither can be chosen after seeing results. Verified end-to-end on 2025-07-28 (140,996 rows) and it reproduces the file-level audit exactly: u_raw +366.5M, u_clip +95.4M.
★ HOW TO READ DIRECTION — three measures, agreement is the rule. (1) NET PREMIUM (buy minus sell) is the robust leg and needs NO new column, it is already implied by the `side` key: each print contributes at most its own premium with a sign, so it is outlier-immune by construction. (2) u_premium_clipped. (3) u_premium raw. MEASURED bucket-level agreement on 2025-07-28 across 45,384 buckets: all three agree on 92.15% of BUCKETS but only 75.33% of PREMIUM; u_raw vs u_clip disagree on just 0.24% of buckets yet those carry 15.8% of premium. ⚠️ THE FRAGILITY IS CONCENTRATED WHERE THE MONEY IS — a count-weighted check would have called this a non-issue. Operating rule: require all three to agree, else ABSTAIN (~25% of premium). Session-level the measures agreed on both sessions tested (2025-07-28 all bullish: net +$553M / u_raw +366M / u_clip +95M; 2026-07-23 bearish: net -$1,025M / u_raw -846M).
CORRECTIONS to the earlier audit row, both overstated: (a) nan_to_num(u, nan=0.0) does NOT corrupt u_premium — u=0 contributes exactly 0.0 to the SUM (verified identical: 366,445,672 both ways). It is a DENOMINATOR hygiene issue only: dividing by a premium total that includes bad-quote prints biases the mean toward zero by their 0.54% weight. (b) Clipping does NOT flip the session-level sign; it changes MAGNITUDE 3.84x (366.4M -> 95.4M). The real risk is per-bucket, quantified above.
⚠️ ANOTHER STRANDED FIX FOUND + PROPAGATED: db/flow_corpus.py's `delete_session_rows` (session-scoped delete before re-roll) existed ONLY in the untracked dev tree. Row-scoped INSERT OR REPLACE is not idempotent here because mny_bucket is in the PRIMARY KEY, so a re-roll that moves a row to a new bucket leaves the old one alive and double-counts the session. Second occurrence of the two-copies trap in one day. VERIFIED the live 2026-07-23 rows are NOT double-counted: 0 split keys, 'unknown' = exactly the index roots (SPX/SPXW/NDXP/NDX/VIX/RUT/XSP/RUTW) at 30.79% of premium, and prints reconcile exactly (11,152,080 - 11,111,194 = 40,886 = unresolved_prints). $45,573M stands.
★ DIRECTION DECISION RULE PRE-REGISTERED + IMPLEMENTED 07-26 — Addendum C (References/FLOW_BASELINE_PREREG_2026-07-26_ADDENDUM_C.md) + signals/options_flow/corpus_direction.py (pure, no I/O, rolling.py discipline) + 8 tests. THE RULE: a bucket is directional only when sign(net_premium), sign(u_premium_clipped) and sign(u_premium) are all non-zero and identical; otherwise ABSTAIN. Abstain is an OUTCOME reported as its own mass — never coerced to neutral, never resolved by preferring whichever measure gives an answer (that is the move the addendum exists to forbid). Zero on any measure abstains, deny-by-default. VALIDATED against the real 2025-07-28 rollup (45,384 buckets): long 40.01% / short 45.84% / abstain 14.15% by COUNT, but abstention = 24.68% BY PREMIUM — inside the pre-declared 20-35% band and matching the audit's 75.33% agreement exactly.
⚠️ Registered honestly as IN-SAMPLE: the rule was chosen after examining 2025-07-28, so that session cannot confirm it. The 20-35%-of-premium abstention band is the pre-declared expectation for the ~258 sessions NOT yet examined; landing outside it is a finding to report, not a reason to retune. Changing the clip bound, going 2-of-3, or adding a fourth measure = schema_version bump + new addendum, NOT a tuning knob.
Two things running it on real data taught us, both now encoded: (1) the dominant dissenter is net_premium (3,456 buckets), NOT raw u (83) — the opposite of the expected failure mode, worth understanding before the study leans on it; (2) 2,858 of 6,421 abstaining buckets are UNANIMOUS ZERO, not conflict — buckets made entirely of at-the-mid prints, where side='unclassified' and u=0 by construction. Those are honestly directionless; conflating them with contested buckets would overstate how contested the corpus is, so DirectionRead.unanimous_abstain separates them.
EMPIRICAL ARM (the part that actually settles which estimator is right): every read carries by_measure — what each of the three would have called on its own, INCLUDING on abstained buckets. Grading those independently is how the outcome ledger ranks the estimators ordinally per calibration-filter-not-goal. ⏳ Wiring these calls into the idea ledger belongs to the STUDY round, not this one — there is no consumer yet and a hook into nothing is dead code. What matters is that the calls are emitted from the start: the comparison cannot be run retroactively.

Addendum D (07-26) — C's central claim was WRONG, and checking it found a contaminant that flips the corpus's sign. C is left in the record unedited; D corrects it. (1) The three measures are ONE signed axis at three weightings, NOT three votes: sign(u) IS the midpoint side by construction (half>0 under good_q), so all three share every print's sign and differ only in weight (1 / min(|u|,1) / |u|). Same-sign measured: raw-vs-clip 99.76%, net-vs-raw 92.20%. Their agreement therefore tests ONLY that direction survives the weighting choice — and a 2-of-3 majority is INCOHERENT, not merely unregistered, because it counts one opinion twice. The majority-vote dissenters() shipped an hour earlier was deleted; abstains now carry a state (no_opinion / weighting_unstable / contested, checked in that order) reported by premium share and NEVER pooled — weighting_unstable is 0.24% of buckets but 15.8% of premium. (2) Consensus cannot see print-level SIGN error, because all three inherit it. Multi-leg allocation legs: 12.96% of prints, 33.33% of premium, and excluding them FLIPS the session sign of all three (net +$553.6M->-$219.3M, clip +$95.4M->-$84.3M, raw +$366.4M->-$176.5M). The 'unanimous long' was unanimous BECAUSE the three share one contaminated sign. multileg is now a GRAIN in the rollup PRIMARY KEY at schema_version=3 — both arms stored, neither presentable alone, one re-roll not a re-purchase. Re-rolled 2025-07-28 in 9s -> 186,768 rows reproducing the standalone measurement exactly. The flag is a HEURISTIC and registered as one: OPRA tcbbo carries no complex-trade condition code (DBN flags is constant 194 across all 6,954,842 prints, tools/tcbbo_flags_probe.py), but ts_event is true-ns so ~1 coincidental collision is expected per session. Raised dbn COLLECTED_PRINTS_MAX 5,000 -> 60,000 (~19s of backlog at this lane's peak, ~9s at whole-market 6,642/s), left the Alpaca constant alone, and fenced the sizing with a test carrying the measurements. ON WHOLE-MARKET: the 30-name watchlist is 43.0% of prints and only 29.4% of premium, so widening is worth ~2.3x the print rate and the bulk of the missing premium — but it is NOT a one-line change: the docstring's 'one variable changes' rule (source, not scope, so a regression is attributable) plus SweepBuffer/RollingFlow/gauge sizing for 6,997 underlyings instead of 30. Own round. ruff clean, 2,864 pass.

2026-07-27h — WHOLE MARKET, live. Founder: 'on our backfill did we download every ticker or just watchlist? We need to see the whole market.' He was right and the answer was embarrassing: backfill = symbols='ALL_SYMBOLS' (6,997 underlyings), live lane = the 30-name flow watchlist. A leftover of the Alpaca architecture (the 1,000-quote cap this vendor was BOUGHT TO REMOVE) that I had defended in the docstring as a deliberate 'one variable changes' constraint — a rationalization, and one that contradicted the standing doctrine that a watchlist is a runtime filter over a fixed-cost feed. TWO OF THE THREE BLOCKERS I CLAIMED WERE WRONG: the pressure gauge self-filters to PRESSURE_UNDERLYINGS so widening never reaches it, and SweepBuffer del's empty buckets so it accumulates no per-contract state. MEASURED cost (2026-03-20): 2.3x prints (peak 6,642/s vs the 60,000 buffer = ~9s backlog), 1.7x sweep events (74.6/min vs 43.1), 1,957,342 mappings = 260 MB RSS, 13.6x CPU headroom. tcbbo is TRADE-DRIVEN (one record per trade + NBBO), so this is the whole US options tape at 438/s average, not a quote firehose. WHAT NARROW COST: 30 names = 43.0% of prints but only 29.4% of PREMIUM — blind to 70% of the tape's dollars while the archive beside it held all of them. ⚠️ TRAP FOUND BY TESTING: databento logs every mapping at INFO from databento.live.client and the collector runs basicConfig(INFO) => 1.96M journal lines PER START. Silenced that logger only; databento.live.protocol stays INFO (slow-reader + symbol-resolution signals live there). Verified end to end off-hours through the real stream class: acked ~17ms, 1,957,349 mapped, data_msgs=0, ZERO callback errors. Empty-watchlist wait + get_subscription_set removed from this lane — nothing to wait for. ruff clean, 2,863 pass.

2026-07-27i — ⚠⚠ THE ARMED LANE RECORDED NOTHING FOR THE FIRST 12 MINUTES OF THE SESSION. Live at 13:30 UTC: data_msgs=161899, mapped=1977981, acks=1, unresolved_syms=0, no errors — and prints=0. CAUSE: databento's OPRA symbology is the 21-char OSI form, 6-char root LEFT-JUSTIFIED AND SPACE-PADDED ('IPI   261218P00050000'); _on_record did str(occ).strip(), which leaves the INTERIOR padding, so _OCC_RE ^([A-Z]{1,6})(\d{6})([CP])(\d{8})$ never matched, meta_for returned None, every print dropped as skipped_no_meta. MEASURED over 2,043,111 real symbols: 0.00% parse as-is, 98.49% with padding removed; residual 1.51% is ~80% adjusted contracts with a digit in the root (WOLF1/SPGI1 — the regex excludes digits) + bare underlying rows that are not contracts. Fixed with occ_from_osi() (removing every space IS the conversion; OSI roots never contain one). LATENT SINCE THE LANE'S FIRST COMMIT, not caused by widening — the corpus rollup was immune because _load_definitions reads the defs file's columns rather than parsing symbols, so a YEAR of backfill validated nothing about the live path, and every off-hours arming check (ack, mappings, liveness, reconnect) passed while the one thing that mattered needed market data to expose. skipped_no_meta was MISSING from the rate line — added. ruff clean, 2,865 pass.

cards.title: Macro regime substrate — keyless Treasury curve + credit spreads, to satisfy a prereg commitment we already made
cards.notes:
Founder 2026-07-26: 'alpaca serves treasury data too... tie that into the system, macro/regime info.'
VERIFIED, not assumed — Alpaca fixed income is real but NOT ours: GET /v1beta1/fixed_income/latest/quotes -> 403 'Subscription does not permit querying fixed income'; broker-api /v1/assets/fixed_income/us_treasuries -> 403 'broker API not available for trade accounts' (partner product). And the SHAPE is wrong regardless: latest quotes only (no history), T-bills first with notes/bonds expanding, i.e. the short end — regime work needs a daily series across the curve. Built for TRADING bonds, not macro context. Do not buy it for this.
★ WHY IT EARNS A CARD RATHER THAN BEING A NICE-TO-HAVE: FLOW_BASELINE_PREREG_2026-07-26 already commits that the event cohort 'must span up, down and sideways regimes; regime composition reported with every result.' We have no regime definition to report against. This closes a hole in a study already on the record.
SOURCES, free + keyless-preferred (data-vs-execution doctrine: never make the product depend on the founder's own vendor accounts): fiscaldata.treasury.gov daily par yield curve 1M-30Y, fully keyless, full history — first choice. FRED (free key) for the axes Treasury does not carry: T10Y2Y, DGS10-DFII10 breakevens, BAMLH0A0HYM2 HY OAS, DTWEXBGS, VIXCLS. Credit spreads are arguably the better regime axis than rates alone — HY OAS widening is what reprices equity risk.
SCOPE: daily regime table (own store, not trading.db), consumed FIRST as prereg regime-composition reporting, only later as a perception input.
⚠️ HONESTY FENCE: regime features fit after the fact trivially. REPORTING cohort composition is fine; SLICING study results by regime is a post-hoc subgroup analysis and requires its own dated addendum before it is run. Never a scored signal without calibration.
SEQUENCING: deliberately NOT started while the OPRA corpus backfill is in flight — that has a rolling-window deadline and this does not, and running both is the many-lanes-at-once failure the founder named himself. Distinct from the done per-symbol-volatility card (per-NAME vol regime, different axis).
